<BEGIN X014>
//! Intents: what an owner signs, and the operation it authorizes.
//!
//! A `transfer` or `repay` intent can run locally (S0), so every field is
//! required and the operation must match what is signed. Family intents, such
//! as `amm.swap_exact_input`, are specified but not run; their fields are
//! optional and only checked for consistency.

use mori_ast::NodeIdx;
use mori_lexer::{TokenIdx, TokenKind, decode_string};
use mori_span::Span;

use crate::checker::Checker;
use crate::declarations::{FieldRole as R, Rules, optional, required};
use crate::values::{ValueIdx, ValueTag};
use crate::{DeclIdx, diagnostics};

/// Largest amount an S0 operation may carry: `2^127 - 1`.
pub const S0_MAX: u128 = (1 << 127) - 1;

/// The fields of a `transfer` or `repay` intent. All are required.
const S0_INTENT: Rules = Rules {
    kind: TokenKind::KwIntent,
    fields: &[
        required("domain", R::Domain),
        required("asset", R::Asset),
        required("signer", R::Account),
        required("key", R::String),
        required("nonce", R::String),
        required("pre_head", R::String),
        required("valid", R::Any),
        required("gross_cap", R::Quantity),
        required("fee_cap", R::Quantity),
        required("net_floor", R::Quantity),
        required("operation", R::Any),
        required("source_hash", R::String),
        required("policy_digest", R::String),
        required("failure", R::Any),
        required("observations", R::Any),
        required("disclosures", R::Any),
        required("retained_effects", R::Any),
        required("retained_duties", R::Any),
        required("delegation", R::Any),
        required("recovery", R::Any),
    ],
};

/// The fields of a family intent. Only `operation` is required.
const FAMILY_INTENT: Rules = Rules {
    kind: TokenKind::KwIntent,
    fields: &[
        required("operation", R::Any),
        optional("authority", R::GrantOrString),
        optional("policy", R::Policy),
        optional("nonce", R::String),
        optional("valid", R::Any),
        optional("reads", R::StringList),
        optional("writes", R::StringList),
        optional("kernel", R::String),
        optional("completion", R::String),
        optional("rounding", R::String),
        optional("relation", R::String),
        optional("failure", R::Any),
        optional("status", R::String),
        optional("observation", R::String),
        optional("continuation", R::String),
        optional("loss", R::String),
        optional("fixing", R::String),
        optional("earliest_round", R::Scalar),
        optional("veto_before", R::Scalar),
        optional("domain", R::Domain),
        optional("asset", R::Asset),
        optional("signer", R::Account),
        optional("key", R::String),
        optional("pre_head", R::String),
        optional("gross_cap", R::Quantity),
        optional("fee_cap", R::Quantity),
        optional("net_floor", R::Quantity),
        optional("source_hash", R::String),
        optional("policy_digest", R::String),
        optional("observations", R::Any),
        optional("disclosures", R::Any),
        optional("retained_effects", R::Any),
        optional("retained_duties", R::StringOrStringList),
        optional("delegation", R::Any),
        optional("recovery", R::Any),
    ],
};

/// Claims an S0 intent binds into what the owner signs; none may be empty.
const S0_CLAIMS: [&str; 5] = ["key", "nonce", "pre_head", "source_hash", "policy_digest"];
const CAPS: [&str; 3] = ["gross_cap", "fee_cap", "net_floor"];

/// What an action's intent can do.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Support {
    /// A `transfer` or `repay`, prepared locally.
    LocalS0,
    /// A family operation: checked, but not run.
    SpecifiedOnly,
}

impl<'a> Checker<'a> {
    /// Checks an intent's fields and its operation. False on any error.
    pub(crate) fn check_intent(&mut self, intent: ValueIdx, value_node: NodeIdx) -> bool {
        let fields = self.field_nodes(value_node);
        let intent_span = self.ast.span(value_node);
        let Some(operation) = self.field(intent, "operation") else {
            self.report(diagnostics::intent_without_operation(intent_span));
            return false;
        };
        let operation_span = self.value_span(&fields, "operation", value_node);
        if self.values.tag(operation) != ValueTag::Call {
            let description = self.describe(operation);
            self.report(diagnostics::operation_not_a_call(
                operation_span,
                &description,
            ));
            return false;
        }
        let name = self.call_name(self.values.node(operation));
        if name.contains('.') {
            return self.check_fields(&FAMILY_INTENT, intent, value_node, &fields)
                && self.check_family_intent(intent, operation, &name, value_node, &fields);
        }
        if !matches!(name.as_str(), "transfer" | "repay") {
            self.report(diagnostics::unsupported_operation(operation_span, &name));
            return false;
        }
        self.check_fields(&S0_INTENT, intent, value_node, &fields)
            && self.check_s0_intent(intent, operation, &name, value_node, &fields)
    }

    fn check_s0_intent(
        &mut self,
        intent: ValueIdx,
        operation: ValueIdx,
        name: &str,
        value_node: NodeIdx,
        fields: &[NodeIdx],
    ) -> bool {
        let mut ok = true;
        let span = |checker: &Self, field: &str| checker.value_span(fields, field, value_node);
        let domain = self
            .values
            .entity(self.field(intent, "domain").expect("checked"));
        let domain_span = span(self, "domain");
        let asset_value = self.field(intent, "asset").expect("checked");
        let asset = self.values.entity(asset_value);
        let signer_value = self.field(intent, "signer").expect("checked");
        let signer = self.values.entity(signer_value);

        for role in ["asset", "signer"] {
            let value = self.field(intent, role).expect("checked");
            ok &= self.check_same_domain(
                value,
                span(self, role),
                role,
                domain,
                domain_span,
                "domain",
            );
        }
        for claim in S0_CLAIMS {
            let value = self.field(intent, claim).expect("checked");
            if self.string_text(value).is_empty() {
                self.report(diagnostics::empty_claim(span(self, claim), claim));
                ok = false;
            }
        }
        ok &= self.check_validity(
            intent,
            span(self, "valid"),
            Some((domain, domain_span)),
            true,
        );
        for cap in CAPS {
            ok &= self.check_amount(
                intent,
                cap,
                span(self, cap),
                asset,
                "it is a cap on the intent's `asset`",
                true,
            );
        }

        let policies: [(&str, &str, Expectation); 7] = [
            ("failure", "SuccessOnly", Expectation::Tag(1)),
            ("observations", "[]", Expectation::EmptyList),
            ("disclosures", "[]", Expectation::EmptyList),
            ("retained_effects", "[]", Expectation::EmptyList),
            ("retained_duties", "[]", Expectation::EmptyList),
            ("delegation", "None", Expectation::Tag(0)),
            ("recovery", "None", Expectation::Tag(0)),
        ];
        for (field, written, expected) in policies {
            let value = self.field(intent, field).expect("checked");
            if !self.matches(value, expected) {
                let description = self.describe(value);
                self.report(diagnostics::s0_policy(
                    span(self, field),
                    field,
                    written,
                    &description,
                ));
                ok = false;
            }
        }

        // The operation must be what the owner signs for.
        let operation_node = self.values.node(operation);
        let arg = |checker: &Self, role: &str| checker.call_arg_span(operation_node, role);
        if name == "transfer" {
            for role in ["from", "to", "fee_to"] {
                let account = self.field(operation, role).expect("checked");
                ok &= self.check_same_domain(
                    account,
                    arg(self, role),
                    role,
                    domain,
                    domain_span,
                    "domain",
                );
            }
            let from = self
                .values
                .entity(self.field(operation, "from").expect("checked"));
            if from != signer {
                self.report(diagnostics::wrong_signer(
                    span(self, "signer"),
                    self.name(signer),
                    "from",
                    self.name(from),
                    arg(self, "from"),
                ));
                ok = false;
            }
            for role in ["value", "fee"] {
                ok &= self.check_amount(
                    operation,
                    role,
                    arg(self, role),
                    asset,
                    "it must be in the intent's `asset`",
                    true,
                );
            }
        } else {
            let loan = self.field(operation, "obligation").expect("checked");
            let loan_span = arg(self, "obligation");
            ok &= self.check_same_domain(
                loan,
                loan_span,
                "obligation",
                domain,
                domain_span,
                "domain",
            );
            if let Some(owed) = self.entity_field(loan, "asset")
                && owed != asset
            {
                let because = format!("the intent's `asset` is `{}`", self.name(asset));
                self.report(diagnostics::wrong_obligation_asset(
                    loan_span,
                    self.name(owed),
                    &because,
                ));
                ok = false;
            }
            let payer = self
                .values
                .entity(self.field(operation, "payer").expect("checked"));
            if payer != signer {
                self.report(diagnostics::wrong_signer(
                    span(self, "signer"),
                    self.name(signer),
                    "payer",
                    self.name(payer),
                    arg(self, "payer"),
                ));
                ok = false;
            }
            ok &= self.check_amount(
                operation,
                "amount",
                arg(self, "amount"),
                asset,
                "it must be in the intent's `asset`",
                true,
            );
        }
        ok
    }

    fn check_family_intent(
        &mut self,
        intent: ValueIdx,
        operation: ValueIdx,
        name: &str,
        value_node: NodeIdx,
        fields: &[NodeIdx],
    ) -> bool {
        let mut ok = true;
        let span = |checker: &Self, field: &str| checker.value_span(fields, field, value_node);
        let operation_node = self.values.node(operation);
        let bridge = name.starts_with("bridge.");

        // The header and the operation's local arguments share one domain.
        let mut header: Vec<(String, ValueIdx, Span)> = Vec::new();
        for role in ["domain", "asset", "signer"] {
            if let Some(value) = self.field(intent, role) {
                header.push((role.to_owned(), value, span(self, role)));
            }
        }
        for (key, value) in self.values.pairs(operation).collect::<Vec<_>>() {
            let role = self.ast.token_text(TokenIdx::new(usize::from(key)));
            if bridge && matches!(role, "source" | "destination") {
                continue;
            }
            header.push((
                role.to_owned(),
                value,
                self.call_arg_span(operation_node, role),
            ));
        }
        let mut domain: Option<(DeclIdx, Span, String)> = None;
        for (role, value, value_span) in &header {
            let Some(this) = self.domain_of(*value) else {
                continue;
            };
            match &domain {
                None => domain = Some((this, *value_span, role.clone())),
                Some((first, first_span, first_role)) => {
                    let (first, first_span, first_role) = (*first, *first_span, first_role.clone());
                    ok &= self.check_same_domain(
                        *value,
                        *value_span,
                        role,
                        first,
                        first_span,
                        &first_role,
                    );
                }
            }
        }

        let bridge_asset = bridge
            .then(|| self.field(operation, "amount"))
            .flatten()
            .filter(|&amount| self.values.tag(amount) == ValueTag::Quantity)
            .map(|amount| self.values.asset(amount));
        let declared = self
            .field(intent, "asset")
            .map(|asset| self.values.entity(asset));
        if let (Some(moved), Some(declared)) = (bridge_asset, declared)
            && moved != declared
        {
            let because = format!(
                "the bridge moves its `amount`, which is in `{}`",
                self.name(moved)
            );
            self.report(diagnostics::wrong_intent_asset(
                span(self, "asset"),
                self.name(declared),
                &because,
            ));
            ok = false;
        }
        let bound = declared.or(bridge_asset);

        let rounds_domain = domain.as_ref().map(|(domain, span, _)| (*domain, *span));
        if self.field(intent, "valid").is_some() {
            ok &= self.check_validity(intent, span(self, "valid"), rounds_domain, false);
        }
        for cap in CAPS {
            let unit = match (cap, name) {
                ("net_floor", "amm.swap_exact_input") => self
                    .field(operation, "output_asset")
                    .map(|asset| self.values.entity(asset)),
                _ => bound,
            };
            if let Some(unit) = unit {
                let because = if cap == "net_floor" && name == "amm.swap_exact_input" {
                    "a swap's floor is measured in its `output_asset`"
                } else {
                    "it is a cap on the intent's asset"
                };
                ok &= self.check_amount(intent, cap, span(self, cap), unit, because, false);
            }
            if let (Some(value), Some((domain, first_span, first_role))) =
                (self.field(intent, cap), &domain)
            {
                let (domain, first_span, first_role) = (*domain, *first_span, first_role.clone());
                ok &= self.check_same_domain(
                    value,
                    span(self, cap),
                    cap,
                    domain,
                    first_span,
                    &first_role,
                );
            }
        }
        ok
    }

    /// `valid` is a `rounds(...)` window on the intent's domain; family
    /// intents may also give two round numbers.
    fn check_validity(
        &mut self,
        intent: ValueIdx,
        span: Span,
        domain: Option<(DeclIdx, Span)>,
        s0: bool,
    ) -> bool {
        let valid = self.field(intent, "valid").expect("validity is present");
        match self.values.tag(valid) {
            ValueTag::Call if self.call_name(self.values.node(valid)) == "rounds" => {
                let window = self.field(valid, "domain").expect("rounds has a domain");
                match domain {
                    Some((domain, domain_span)) => {
                        self.check_same_domain(window, span, "valid", domain, domain_span, "domain")
                    }
                    None => true,
                }
            }
            ValueTag::List if !s0 => {
                let items: Vec<ValueIdx> = self.values.items(valid).collect();
                let scalars = items
                    .iter()
                    .all(|&item| self.values.tag(item) == ValueTag::Scalar);
                if items.len() == 2 && scalars {
                    return true;
                }
                self.report(diagnostics::invalid_validity(span, s0));
                false
            }
            _ => {
                self.report(diagnostics::invalid_validity(span, s0));
                false
            }
        }
    }

    /// The field `role` of `value`, when present, is an amount of `asset`,
    /// within the S0 maximum when `s0` is set.
    fn check_amount(
        &mut self,
        value: ValueIdx,
        role: &str,
        span: Span,
        asset: DeclIdx,
        because: &str,
        s0: bool,
    ) -> bool {
        let Some(amount) = self.field(value, role) else {
            return true;
        };
        let actual = self.values.asset(amount);
        if actual != asset {
            let what = format!("`{role}`");
            self.report(diagnostics::wrong_asset(
                span,
                &what,
                self.name(asset),
                self.name(actual),
                because,
            ));
            return false;
        }
        if s0 && self.values.amount(amount) > S0_MAX {
            self.report(diagnostics::too_large_for_s0(span, role));
            return false;
        }
        true
    }

    fn matches(&self, value: ValueIdx, expected: Expectation) -> bool {
        match expected {
            Expectation::Tag(tag) => {
                self.values.tag(value) == ValueTag::Tag
                    && self.values.rows.a()[value.index()] == tag
            }
            Expectation::EmptyList => {
                self.values.tag(value) == ValueTag::List
                    && self.values.items(value).next().is_none()
            }
        }
    }

    fn string_text(&self, value: ValueIdx) -> String {
        let token = TokenIdx::new(usize::from(self.values.rows.a()[value.index()]));
        decode_string(self.ast.token_text(token))
    }

    /// The span of argument `role` of the call at `node`, or the whole value
    /// when the call is not written out there.
    fn call_arg_span(&self, node: NodeIdx, role: &str) -> Span {
        if self.ast.tag(node) == mori_ast::NodeTag::Call
            && let Some(field) = self
                .ast
                .list(node)
                .find(|&field| self.ast.token_text(self.ast.main_token(field)) == role)
        {
            return self.ast.span(self.operand(field, 0));
        }
        self.ast.span(node)
    }

    /// What the action's intent can do, from its operation.
    pub(crate) fn support(&self, intent: DeclIdx) -> Option<Support> {
        let value = self.declarations.value()[intent.index()]?;
        let operation = self.field(value, "operation")?;
        let name = self.call_name(self.values.node(operation));
        Some(if name.contains('.') {
            Support::SpecifiedOnly
        } else {
            Support::LocalS0
        })
    }
}

/// A value an S0 intent requires exactly.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum Expectation {
    /// The tag `None` (`0`) or `SuccessOnly` (`1`).
    Tag(u16),
    EmptyList,
}
<END X014>

<BEGIN X015>
//! Checks a parsed `moriarty-beta/1` file.
//!
//! [`check`] walks the agreement's items in order, and each declaration sees
//! only the declarations above it. A declaration with an error is marked
//! failed, and anything that depends on it is skipped without further errors,
//! so each mistake is reported once.

mod calls;
mod checker;
mod declarations;
mod diagnostics;
mod eval;
mod intents;
mod names;
mod relations;
mod reserved;
mod types;
mod values;

#[cfg(test)]
mod proptests;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use mori_ast::{Ast, NodeIdx};
use mori_diagnostics::MoriDiagnostic;
use mori_lexer::TokenKind;
use soa_rs::{Soa, Soars};

pub use checker::check;
pub use intents::Support;
pub use values::{Value, ValueIdx, ValueTag, Values};

/// Everything [`check`] could check, and every error it found. The program
/// is accepted only when there are no diagnostics.
pub struct CheckResult<'a> {
    pub checked: Checked<'a>,
    pub diagnostics: Vec<MoriDiagnostic>,
}

impl CheckResult<'_> {
    pub fn is_accepted(&self) -> bool {
        self.diagnostics.is_empty()
    }
}

/// Index of a declaration in [`Checked`]. An agreement has at most 256 items.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct DeclIdx(u16);

impl DeclIdx {
    pub fn new(index: usize) -> Self {
        Self(u16::try_from(index).expect("declaration index exceeds u16"))
    }

    pub fn index(self) -> usize {
        usize::from(self.0)
    }
}

/// A declaration, in source order.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Soars)]
#[soa_derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Declaration {
    pub node: NodeIdx,
    /// It has an error, or depends on a declaration that does.
    pub failed: bool,
    /// Its value, unless it failed.
    pub value: Option<ValueIdx>,
}

/// An action, in source order.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Soars)]
#[soa_derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Action {
    pub node: NodeIdx,
    /// The intent it uses, when that resolved to an intent declaration.
    pub intent: Option<DeclIdx>,
    /// What that intent can do, when it was checked.
    pub support: Option<Support>,
}

/// The checked program, as side tables over the [`Ast`].
pub struct Checked<'a> {
    pub ast: &'a Ast<'a>,
    pub declarations: Soa<Declaration>,
    pub actions: Soa<Action>,
    pub values: Values,
    /// For each node, the declaration it names: a reference, a quantity's
    /// asset or an action's intent. [`UNRESOLVED`] otherwise.
    resolutions: Vec<u16>,
}

const UNRESOLVED: u16 = u16::MAX;

impl<'a> Checked<'a> {
    /// The keyword that declared it, such as [`TokenKind::KwConst`].
    pub fn kind(&self, decl: DeclIdx) -> TokenKind {
        let node = self.declarations.node()[decl.index()];
        self.ast.tokens.kind(self.ast.main_token(node))
    }

    /// The value of a declaration that did not fail.
    pub fn value(&self, decl: DeclIdx) -> Option<ValueIdx> {
        self.declarations.value()[decl.index()]
    }

    pub fn name(&self, decl: DeclIdx) -> &'a str {
        let node = self.declarations.node()[decl.index()];
        self.ast
            .token_text(self.ast.token_after(self.ast.main_token(node), 1))
    }

    /// The declaration `node` names, if it is a reference, quantity or action
    /// that resolved.
    pub fn resolution(&self, node: NodeIdx) -> Option<DeclIdx> {
        let raw = self.resolutions[node.index()];
        (raw != UNRESOLVED).then_some(DeclIdx(raw))
    }
}

use crate::*;
use mori_lexer::{TokenIdx, TokenKind};

/// Parses the explicitly versioned core profile; beta grammar is untouched.
pub fn parse(source: &str) -> Result<Program, Error> {
    parse_profile(source, false)
}

/// Syntax-only parser; only stage::load admits the resulting source.
pub(crate) fn parse_v2(source: &str) -> Result<Program, Error> {
    parse_profile(source, true)
}

fn parse_profile(source: &str, staged: bool) -> Result<Program, Error> {
    let lexed = mori_lexer::lex(source).map_err(|e| Error::new("lex", e.to_string()))?;
    let tokens = (0..lexed.len())
        .map(|i| {
            let idx = TokenIdx::new(i);
            let span = lexed.span(idx, source);
            let raw = &source[span.start as usize..span.end as usize];
            let text = if lexed.kind(idx) == TokenKind::String {
                mori_lexer::decode_string(raw)
            } else {
                raw.to_owned()
            };
            Tok {
                text,
                kind: lexed.kind(idx),
                start: span.start,
            }
        })
        .collect();
    let mut parser = Parser {
        tokens,
        pos: 0,
        program: Program {
            language: if staged {
                crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2
            } else {
                LANGUAGE
            }
            .into(),
            semantics: if staged {
                crate::stage::SEMANTICS_2
            } else {
                SEMANTICS
            }
            .into(),
            name: String::new(),
            states: vec![],
            assets: vec![],
            expressions: vec![],
            actions: vec![],
        },
    };
    parser.expect("language")?;
    let profile = parser.string()?;
    let expected_language = if staged {
        crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2
    } else {
        LANGUAGE
    };
    if profile != expected_language {
        return Err(parser.error(
            "profile",
            format!("Expected language \"{expected_language}\"; found {profile:?}."),
        ));
    }
    parser.expect(";")?;
    parser.expect("agreement")?;
    parser.program.name = parser.word()?;
    parser.expect("{")?;
    while !parser.eat("}") {
        if parser.eat("state") {
            let name = parser.word()?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let ty = parser.ty()?;
            parser.expect("=")?;
            let initial = parser.literal()?;
            parser.expect(";")?;
            parser.program.states.push(StateDecl { name, ty, initial });
        } else if parser.eat("asset") {
            let name = parser.word()?;
            parser.expect("=")?;
            parser.expect("{")?;
            parser.expect("network")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let network = parser.string()?;
            parser.expect(",")?;
            parser.expect("issuer")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let issuer = parser.string()?;
            parser.expect(",")?;
            parser.expect("reference")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let reference = parser.string()?;
            parser.expect(",")?;
            parser.expect("scale")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let Value::UInt(UInt(scale)) = parser.literal()? else {
                return Err(parser.error("asset", "Asset scale must be an unsigned integer."));
            };
            let scale = u8::try_from(scale)
                .map_err(|_| parser.error("asset", "Asset scale must fit u8."))?;
            parser.eat(",");
            parser.expect("}")?;
            parser.expect(";")?;
            parser.program.assets.push(AssetDecl {
                name,
                identity: AssetId {
                    network,
                    issuer,
                    reference,
                    scale,
                },
            });
        } else if parser.eat("action") {
            let name = parser.word()?;
            parser.expect("(")?;
            let mut inputs = vec![];
            if !parser.eat(")") {
                loop {
                    let name = parser.word()?;
                    parser.expect(":")?;
                    let ty = parser.ty()?;
                    inputs.push(InputDecl { name, ty });
                    if parser.eat(")") {
                        break;
                    }
                    parser.expect(",")?;
                }
            }
            parser.expect("{")?;
            let mut statements = vec![];
            while !parser.eat("}") {
                if parser.eat("input") {
                    if !statements.is_empty() {
                        return Err(
                            parser.error("input", "Declare action inputs before statements.")
                        );
                    }
                    let name = parser.word()?;
                    parser.expect(":")?;
                    let ty = parser.ty()?;
                    parser.expect(";")?;
                    inputs.push(InputDecl { name, ty });
                    continue;
                }
                statements.push(parser.statement()?);
                if statements.len() > MAX_STATEMENTS {
                    return Err(parser.error("bound", "Action exceeds 1,024 statements."));
                }
            }
            parser.program.actions.push(Action {
                name,
                inputs,
                statements,
            });
        } else {
            return Err(parser.error("unsupported", "Expected state, asset or action declaration; loops and native calls are unsupported."));
        }
        if parser.program.states.len() + parser.program.assets.len() + parser.program.actions.len()
            > MAX_DECLARATIONS
        {
            return Err(parser.error("bound", "Program exceeds 256 declarations."));
        }
    }
    if parser.peek().kind != TokenKind::Eof {
        return Err(parser.error("syntax", "Unexpected content after agreement."));
    }
    if !staged {
        validate(&parser.program)?;
    }
    Ok(parser.program)
}
struct Tok {
    text: String,
    kind: TokenKind,
    start: u32,
}
struct Parser {
    tokens: Vec<Tok>,
    pos: usize,
    program: Program,
}
impl Parser {
    fn peek(&self) -> &Tok {
        &self.tokens[self.pos]
    }
    fn error(&self, code: &str, message: impl Into<String>) -> Error {
        let mut e = Error::new(code, message);
        e.offset = Some(self.peek().start);
        e
    }
    fn eat(&mut self, text: &str) -> bool {
        if self.peek().text == text && self.peek().kind != TokenKind::String {
            self.pos += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }
    fn expect(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if self.eat(text) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(self.error(
                "syntax",
                format!("Expected {text:?}; found {:?}.", self.peek().text),
            ))
        }
    }
    fn word(&mut self) -> Result<String, Error> {
        if self.peek().kind.is_word() {
            let text = self.peek().text.clone();
            self.pos += 1;
            Ok(text)
        } else {
            Err(self.error("syntax", "Expected a name."))
        }
    }
    fn string(&mut self) -> Result<String, Error> {
        if self.peek().kind == TokenKind::String {
            let text = self.peek().text.clone();
            self.pos += 1;
            Ok(text)
        } else {
            Err(self.error("syntax", "Expected a quoted string."))
        }
    }
    fn ty(&mut self) -> Result<Type, Error> {
        match self.word()?.as_str() {
            "UInt" => Ok(Type::UInt),
            "Bool" => Ok(Type::Bool),
            _ => Err(self.error("type", "Supported types are UInt and Bool.")),
        }
    }
    fn literal(&mut self) -> Result<Value, Error> {
        if self.eat("true") {
            return Ok(Value::Bool(true));
        }
        if self.eat("false") {
            return Ok(Value::Bool(false));
        }
        if self.peek().kind != TokenKind::Number {
            return Err(self.error("syntax", "Expected an unsigned integer or boolean literal."));
        }
        let raw = self.peek().text.replace('_', "");
        let n = raw.parse::<u128>().map_err(|_| {
            self.error(
                "number",
                "UInt literal must fit u128; amounts use integral atomic units.",
            )
        })?;
        self.pos += 1;
        Ok(Value::UInt(UInt(n)))
    }
    fn push(&mut self, expr: Expr) -> Result<ExprId, Error> {
        if self.program.expressions.len() >= MAX_EXPRESSIONS {
            return Err(self.error("bound", "Program exceeds 8,192 expression nodes."));
        }
        let id = self.program.expressions.len() as u16;
        self.program.expressions.push(expr);
        Ok(id)
    }
    fn expr(&mut self, minimum: u8, depth: usize) -> Result<ExprId, Error> {
        if depth > 64 {
            return Err(self.error("bound", "Expression nesting exceeds 64."));
        }
        let mut lhs = if self.eat("(") {
            let e = self.expr(0, depth + 1)?;
            self.expect(")")?;
            e
        } else if self.eat("not") {
            let value = self.expr(6, depth + 1)?;
            self.push(Expr::Not { value })?
        } else if self.peek().kind == TokenKind::Number
            || self.peek().text == "true"
            || self.peek().text == "false"
        {
            let value = self.literal()?;
            self.push(Expr::Literal { value })?
        } else {
            let name = self.word()?;
            if matches!(name.as_str(), "liability_present" | "liability_amount") && self.eat("(") {
                let duty = self.string()?;
                self.expect(")")?;
                self.push(if name == "liability_present" {
                    Expr::LiabilityPresent { name: duty }
                } else {
                    Expr::LiabilityAmount { name: duty }
                })?
            } else {
                self.push(Expr::Name { name })?
            }
        };
        loop {
            // A decoded string spelling an operator is still a string token.
            if self.peek().kind == TokenKind::String {
                break;
            }
            let next = self
                .tokens
                .get(self.pos + 1)
                .filter(|t| t.kind != TokenKind::String)
                .map(|t| t.text.as_str());
            let (op, precedence, length) = match (self.peek().text.as_str(), next) {
                ("or", _) => (BinaryOp::Or, 1, 1),
                ("and", _) => (BinaryOp::And, 2, 1),
                ("=", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Eq, 3, 2),
                ("not", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Ne, 3, 2),
                ("<", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Le, 3, 2),
                (">", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Ge, 3, 2),
                ("<", _) => (BinaryOp::Lt, 3, 1),
                (">", _) => (BinaryOp::Gt, 3, 1),
                ("+", _) => (BinaryOp::Add, 4, 1),
                ("-", _) => (BinaryOp::Sub, 4, 1),
                ("*", _) => (BinaryOp::Mul, 5, 1),
                _ => break,
            };
            if precedence < minimum {
                break;
            }
            self.pos += length;
            let rhs = self.expr(precedence + 1, depth + 1)?;
            lhs = self.push(Expr::Binary { op, lhs, rhs })?;
        }
        Ok(lhs)
    }
    fn statement(&mut self) -> Result<Statement, Error> {
        let keyword = self.word()?;
        let s=match keyword.as_str() {
            "await" if self.program.language == crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2 => {
                let label = self.word()?;
                self.expect("(")?;
                let mut binders = Vec::new();
                if !self.eat(")") {
                    loop {
                        let name = self.word()?;
                        self.expect(":")?;
                        let ty = self.ty()?;
                        binders.push(InputDecl { name, ty });
                        if self.eat(")") { break; }
                        self.expect(",")?;
                    }
                }
                self.expect("when")?;
                Statement::Await { label, binders, guard: self.expr(0, 0)? }
            },
            "let"=>{let name=self.word()?;self.expect("=")?;Statement::Let{name,value:self.expr(0,0)?}},
            "next"=>{let state=self.word()?;self.expect("=")?;Statement::Next{state,value:self.expr(0,0)?}},
            "requires"=>Statement::Requires{predicate:self.expr(0,0)?},
            "ensures"=>Statement::Ensures{predicate:self.expr(0,0)?},
            "emit"=>{let name=self.string()?;self.expect("(")?;let value=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;Statement::Emit{name,value}},
            "transfer"|"fee"=>{self.expect("(")?;let asset=self.word()?;self.expect(",")?;let from=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let to=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let amount=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;if keyword=="fee"{Statement::Fee{asset,from,to,amount}}else{Statement::Transfer{asset,from,to,amount}}},
            "liability"=>{self.expect("(")?;let name=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let asset=self.word()?;self.expect(",")?;let debtor=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let creditor=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let amount=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;Statement::Liability{name,asset,debtor,creditor,amount}},
            "discharge"=>{self.expect("(")?;let name=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let amount=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;Statement::Discharge{name,amount}},
            _=>return Err(self.error("unsupported",format!("Unsupported statement {keyword:?}; use let, requires, ensures, next, emit, transfer, fee, liability or discharge."))),
        };
        self.expect(";")?;
        Ok(s)
    }
}

/// Read the explicit source profile for CLI routing; this does not admit a program.
pub fn language(source: &str) -> Result<&'static str, Error> {
    let lexed = mori_lexer::lex(source).map_err(|e| Error::new("lex", e.to_string()))?;
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..lexed.len() {
        let idx = TokenIdx::new(i);
        let span = lexed.span(idx, source);
        let raw = &source[span.start as usize..span.end as usize];
        let kind = lexed.kind(idx);
        tokens.push(Tok {
            text: if kind == TokenKind::String {
                mori_lexer::decode_string(raw)
            } else {
                raw.to_owned()
            },
            kind,
            start: span.start,
        });
    }
    let mut parser = Parser {
        tokens,
        pos: 0,
        program: Program {
            language: LANGUAGE.into(),
            semantics: SEMANTICS.into(),
            name: String::new(),
            states: vec![],
            assets: vec![],
            expressions: vec![],
            actions: vec![],
        },
    };
    let expected = format!(
        "language \"{LANGUAGE}\" or \"{}\"",
        crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2
    );
    parser.expect("language").map_err(|mut error| {
        error.message = format!("Expected {expected}. {}", error.message);
        error
    })?;
    let profile = parser.string().map_err(|mut error| {
        error.message = format!("Expected {expected}. {}", error.message);
        error
    })?;
    match profile.as_str() {
        LANGUAGE => Ok(LANGUAGE),
        crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2 => Ok(crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2),
        _ => Err(parser.error(
            "profile",
            format!("Expected {expected}; found {profile:?}."),
        )),
    }
}

//! Strict bounded decoding of local stage files and the R7 canonical boundary.
//!
//! Size limits apply to bytes actually read, before parsing. Parsing keeps the
//! legacy duplicate-key, depth and node limits; only the byte ceiling differs.
//! A resumed boundary is checked as written and is never re-sorted.
use super::{Continuation, NamedValue, StageEvent, StagedProgram};
use crate::{AssetId, Error, MAX_TRACE_CELLS, Program, Snapshot, Statement};
use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::Path;

pub use super::{MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES, MAX_EVENT_BYTES};

pub const CONTINUATION_TOO_LARGE: &str = "Continuation JSON exceeds 4 MiB";
pub const EVENT_TOO_LARGE: &str = "Stage event JSON exceeds 64 KiB";

/// Reads at most `max + 1` bytes, so the limit holds even if the file grows
/// after it is opened. Oversized or non-UTF-8 input fails with `json`.
pub fn read_bounded(path: &Path, max: usize, too_large: &'static str) -> Result<String, Error> {
    use std::io::Read;
    let file = std::fs::File::open(path)
        .map_err(|e| Error::new("io", format!("Cannot open stage input: {e}")))?;
    let limit = u64::try_from(max).unwrap_or(u64::MAX).saturating_add(1);
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    file.take(limit)
        .read_to_end(&mut bytes)
        .map_err(|e| Error::new("io", format!("Cannot read stage input: {e}")))?;
    if bytes.len() > max {
        return Err(Error::new("json", too_large));
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| Error::new("json", "Stage input is not UTF-8"))
}

fn strict<T: DeserializeOwned>(
    text: &str,
    max: usize,
    too_large: &'static str,
) -> Result<T, Error> {
    let value = crate::json::parse_limited(text, max, too_large)?;
    serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|e| Error::new("json", e.to_string()))
}

/// Exactly one `Continuation`; unknown fields, a missing `cap` key and
/// non-canonical UInt strings are rejected by the type's derives.
pub fn continuation(text: &str) -> Result<Continuation, Error> {
    strict(text, MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES, CONTINUATION_TOO_LARGE)
}

pub fn event(text: &str) -> Result<StageEvent, Error> {
    strict(text, MAX_EVENT_BYTES, EVENT_TOO_LARGE)
}

type Identity<'a> = (&'a AssetId, &'a str, &'a str);

/// Source-fixed liability identities over every action of the program.
fn registry(p: &Program) -> Result<BTreeMap<&str, Identity<'_>>, Error> {
    let mut identities = BTreeMap::new();
    for stmt in p.actions.iter().flat_map(|action| &action.statements) {
        if let Statement::Liability {
            name,
            asset,
            debtor,
            creditor,
            ..
        } = stmt
        {
            let id = asset_identity(p, asset)?;
            let identity = (id, debtor.as_str(), creditor.as_str());
            if identities
                .insert(name.as_str(), identity)
                .is_some_and(|existing| existing != identity)
            {
                return Err(Error::new(
                    "liability",
                    format!("Conflicting source liability identity for {name:?}."),
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(identities)
}

fn asset_identity<'a>(p: &'a Program, name: &str) -> Result<&'a AssetId, Error> {
    p.assets
        .iter()
        .find(|a| a.name == name)
        .map(|a| &a.identity)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("asset", format!("Unknown asset {name:?}.")))
}

/// R7: the legacy `scenario_snapshot` predicates applied to a resumed boundary
/// without normalisation. Codes and messages follow `scenario_snapshot`;
/// ordering failures are new `balance`/`liability` messages.
///
/// Balances keep the baseline predicate: every account the whole action
/// transfers from or to must be present, and other declared-asset accounts
/// (such as an untouched observer) are preserved, not refused.
pub fn canonical_boundary(
    sp: &StagedProgram,
    action: usize,
    captures: &[NamedValue],
    b: &Snapshot,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let p = sp.program();
    let (Some(a), Some(plan)) = (p.actions.get(action), sp.plan().actions.get(action)) else {
        return Err(Error::new("stage_site", "Unknown staged action."));
    };
    // (d) Snapshot has no inputs component (U-1); R4 alone binds captures.
    let _ = captures;
    if b.balances.len() > 4096 || b.liabilities.len() > 1024 {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "bound",
            "Scenario exceeds 4,096 balances or 1,024 liabilities.",
        ));
    }
    // (a) States: exactly the declared states, each of its declared type.
    if b.state.len() != p.states.len() {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "state",
            "Boundary must provide every declared state value and no other.",
        ));
    }
    for d in &p.states {
        let value = b
            .state
            .get(&d.name)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("state", format!("Missing state {:?}.", d.name)))?;
        if value.ty() != d.ty {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "state",
                format!("Wrong type for state {:?}.", d.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    // (b) Balances: declared assets, valid accounts, strictly ascending by
    // (asset, account), which also excludes duplicates.
    let ids: BTreeSet<&AssetId> = p.assets.iter().map(|a| &a.identity).collect();
    let mut previous: Option<(&AssetId, &str)> = None;
    for balance in &b.balances {
        if !ids.contains(&balance.asset) {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "asset",
                format!(
                    "Undeclared exact asset identity for account {:?}.",
                    balance.account
                ),
            ));
        }
        if balance.account.is_empty() || balance.account.len() > 1024 {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "balance",
                "Duplicate or invalid balance account/asset.",
            ));
        }
        let key = (&balance.asset, balance.account.as_str());
        if previous.is_some_and(|prior| prior >= key) {
            return Err(Error::new("balance", "Balances are not canonical"));
        }
        previous = Some(key);
    }
    for stmt in &a.statements {
        if let Statement::Transfer {
            asset, from, to, ..
        }
        | Statement::Fee {
            asset, from, to, ..
        } = stmt
        {
            let id = asset_identity(p, asset)?;
            for account in [from, to] {
                if b.balances
                    .binary_search_by(|x| {
                        (&x.asset, x.account.as_str()).cmp(&(id, account.as_str()))
                    })
                    .is_err()
                {
                    return Err(Error::new(
                        "balance",
                        format!("Missing explicit balance for {account:?} and asset {asset:?}."),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // (c) Liabilities: strictly ascending by name; every name is a source
    // liability of this program with exactly its registered identity.
    let registry = registry(p)?;
    let mut previous: Option<&str> = None;
    for l in &b.liabilities {
        if !ids.contains(&l.asset) {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "asset",
                "Liability uses undeclared exact asset identity.",
            ));
        }
        if l.name.is_empty()
            || l.name.len() > 1024
            || l.debtor.is_empty()
            || l.creditor.is_empty()
            || l.debtor.len() > 1024
            || l.creditor.len() > 1024
        {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "liability",
                "Invalid or duplicate liability identity.",
            ));
        }
        if previous.is_some_and(|prior| prior >= l.name.as_str()) {
            return Err(Error::new("liability", "Liabilities are not canonical"));
        }
        previous = Some(l.name.as_str());
        if registry.get(l.name.as_str())
            != Some(&(&l.asset, l.debtor.as_str(), l.creditor.as_str()))
        {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "liability",
                format!("Existing liability identity differs for {:?}.", l.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    // (e) Trace cells over the whole action, as at start.
    let added = a
        .statements
        .iter()
        .filter(|stmt| matches!(stmt, Statement::Liability { .. }))
        .count();
    let records = p.states.len() + b.balances.len() + b.liabilities.len() + added + 1;
    if records.saturating_mul(usize::from(plan.statement_count) + 2) > MAX_TRACE_CELLS {
        return Err(Error::new(
            "bound",
            "Scenario and action exceed 65,536 trace snapshot records.",
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

//! Staged `moriarty/2` programs and their local continuation interface.
//!
//! Local and unsigned only. Event binders and captures are caller-chosen values
//! (no authentication), a continuation can be resumed any number of times (no
//! consumption tracking), and no stage authority exists. Outputs carry
//! `STAGE_LABELS` so these limits stay visible.
mod admit;
mod cost;
pub mod decode;
mod digest;
#[cfg(feature = "core2-disjoint-draft")]
pub mod disjoint;
mod plan;
mod profile;
mod report;
mod validate;

pub use crate::LOGICAL_COST_PROFILE_2;
pub use admit::{resume, start};
pub use plan::{ActionPlan, AwaitSite, CaptureSlot, Origin, StageBinder, StagePlan};
pub use profile::{require_core1, require_core2};
pub use report::outcome_report;

use crate::{Error, Execution, Liability, Program, Snapshot, UInt, Value};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

pub const LANGUAGE_2: &str = "moriarty/2";
pub const SEMANTICS_2: &str = "moriarty-core/2";
pub const STAGE_PLAN_FORMAT: &str = "moriarty-stage-plan/1";
pub const CONTINUATION_FORMAT: &str = "moriarty-continuation/1";
pub const STAGE_EVENT_FORMAT: &str = "moriarty-stage-event/1";
pub const MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION: usize = 16;
pub const MAX_EVENT_BINDERS: usize = 16;
pub const MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS: usize = 256;
pub const MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1_048_576;
pub const MAX_EVENT_BYTES: usize = 65_536;
/// Inserted verbatim into every `/2` output object.
pub const STAGE_LABELS: [(&str, &str); 3] = [
    ("qualification", "local-reference-stage"),
    ("authentication", "none"),
    ("consumption", "untracked"),
];

/// A `/2` program that passed profile, validation, plan invariants and static
/// costing, with its canonical digests. Only `load` constructs one; there is
/// no public constructor, `Default` or `Deserialize`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StagedProgram {
    program: Program,
    plan: StagePlan,
    program_hash: [u8; 32],
    plan_hash: [u8; 32],
}
impl StagedProgram {
    pub fn program(&self) -> &Program {
        &self.program
    }
    pub fn plan(&self) -> &StagePlan {
        &self.plan
    }
    pub fn program_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        self.program_hash
    }
    pub fn plan_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        self.plan_hash
    }
    /// Declaration index of an action; plan and program actions share it.
    pub(crate) fn action_index(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.program.actions.iter().position(|a| a.name == name)
    }
}

/// Parses, admits and plans a `moriarty/2` source. Legacy `parse`/`validate`
/// remain `/1`-only, so a `/2` source fails every legacy consumer.
pub fn load(src: &str) -> Result<StagedProgram, Error> {
    let program = crate::parser::parse_v2(src)?;
    profile::require_core2(&program)?;
    validate::validate_v2(&program)?;
    let mut plan = plan::build(&program)?;
    validate::plan_invariants(&program, &plan)?;
    cost::fill(&program, &mut plan)?;
    validate::cost_invariants(&program, &plan)?;
    let program_hash = digest::program_hash(&program)?;
    plan.program_hash = digest::hex(&program_hash);
    let plan_hash = digest::plan_hash(&plan)?;
    Ok(StagedProgram {
        program,
        plan,
        program_hash,
        plan_hash,
    })
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct NamedValue {
    pub name: String,
    pub value: Value,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct StageLogical {
    pub profile: String,
    /// Mandatory key; `None` is written as `null`.
    #[serde(deserialize_with = "Option::deserialize")]
    pub cap: Option<UInt>,
    pub committed: UInt,
}
/// Resume input. `site` and `captures` are the executing action's pending
/// frame; `boundary` is the legacy Snapshot. Nothing here is authenticated.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Continuation {
    pub format: String,
    pub program_hash: String,
    pub plan_hash: String,
    pub action: String,
    pub site: u16,
    pub captures: Vec<NamedValue>,
    pub logical: StageLogical,
    pub boundary: Snapshot,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct StageEvent {
    pub format: String,
    pub action: String,
    pub label: String,
    pub values: Vec<NamedValue>,
}
/// Local frame of one action. `site == 0` exactly when `captures` is empty
/// and the action is idle; no padding is represented locally.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PendingFrame {
    pub site: u16,
    pub captures: Vec<NamedValue>,
}
impl PendingFrame {
    pub(crate) fn idle() -> Self {
        Self {
            site: 0,
            captures: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}
/// Output only. Segment history is never decoded or trusted on resume, so no
/// `Deserialize` exists over the shared Await-bearing `Statement`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct StageSegment {
    pub action: String,
    pub frame_pre: PendingFrame,
    pub frame_post: PendingFrame,
    pub execution: Execution,
}
/// `residual` lists every post-boundary liability with a positive amount, in
/// the existing complete `Liability` representation.
// Public outcome; boxing `Waiting` would change every caller's pattern.
#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum StageOutcome {
    Waiting {
        advanced: bool,
        segment: Option<StageSegment>,
        continuation: Continuation,
        attempted: UInt,
        residual: Vec<Liability>,
    },
    Complete {
        segment: StageSegment,
        committed: UInt,
        attempted: UInt,
        residual: Vec<Liability>,
    },
}
/// A rejected invocation publishes no segment, effects or continuation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{error}")]
pub struct StageRejection {
    pub error: Error,
    pub attempted: UInt,
    pub committed: UInt,
}

/// Positive residual duties of a boundary, in its (name-sorted) order.
pub(crate) fn residual(snapshot: &Snapshot) -> Vec<Liability> {
    snapshot
        .liabilities
        .iter()
        .filter(|l| l.amount.0 > 0)
        .cloned()
        .collect()
}

//! Profile isolation between `moriarty-core/1` and `moriarty-core/2` consumers.
//! Both helpers keep the existing `mori::core::profile` error identity.
use super::{LANGUAGE_2, SEMANTICS_2};
use crate::{Error, LANGUAGE, Program, SEMANTICS, Statement};

const PROFILE_MESSAGE: &str = "Unsupported language or semantics identity.";

/// Required at every `/1` entry point before evaluation or layout. An
/// in-memory program labelled `/1` that still carries an Await is refused.
pub fn require_core1(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE || program.semantics != SEMANTICS {
        return Err(Error::new("profile", PROFILE_MESSAGE));
    }
    if program
        .actions
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|action| &action.statements)
        .any(|statement| matches!(statement, Statement::Await { .. }))
    {
        return Err(Error::new("profile", "Await requires moriarty-core/2."));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Required at every staged entry point; `/1` programs are refused.
pub fn require_core2(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE_2 || program.semantics != SEMANTICS_2 {
        return Err(Error::new("profile", PROFILE_MESSAGE));
    }
    Ok(())
}
<END X028>

<BEGIN X029>
//! Complete qualified JSON envelopes for the local Core/2 outcome API.
use super::{STAGE_LABELS, StageOutcome, StageRejection};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

/// Render an outcome or rejection without executing a program or performing I/O.
/// Every envelope retains the explicit local-stage qualifications.
pub fn outcome_report(result: Result<StageOutcome, StageRejection>) -> Value {
    let mut report = match result {
        Ok(StageOutcome::Waiting {
            advanced,
            segment,
            continuation,
            attempted,
            residual,
        }) => {
            let committed = continuation.logical.committed;
            json!({"status":"waiting","advanced":advanced,"segment":segment,
                "continuation":continuation,"attempted":attempted,
                "committed":committed,"residual":residual})
        }
        Ok(StageOutcome::Complete {
            segment,
            committed,
            attempted,
            residual,
        }) => json!({"status":"complete","segment":segment,"attempted":attempted,
                "committed":committed,"residual":residual}),
        Err(rejected) => json!({"status":"rejected","error":rejected.error,
            "attempted":rejected.attempted,"committed":rejected.committed}),
    };
    let object = report
        .as_object_mut()
        .expect("stage reports are JSON objects");
    for (name, value) in STAGE_LABELS {
        object.insert(name.into(), Value::String(value.into()));
    }
    report
}
<END X029>

## X030: crates/mori-core/src/stage/validate.rs

<BEGIN X030>
//! `/2` static validation and stage plan invariants.
//!
//! `validate_v2` applies every legacy `/1` program check with the legacy codes
//! and messages, plus the Await rules: top-level placement (structural in IR),
//! unique labels, non-shadowing binders, Bool guards typed over the prefix and
//! the Await's own binders, the per-action bounds, and `await`/`when` reserved.
//! Legacy `validate` is unchanged and remains `/1`-only.
use super::{
    AwaitSite, CaptureSlot, LANGUAGE_2, MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION, MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS,
    MAX_EVENT_BINDERS, Origin, SEMANTICS_2, STAGE_PLAN_FORMAT, StageBinder, StagePlan,
};
use crate::runtime::{
    expr_type, identifier, require_uint, validate_asset, validate_liability_reads,
};
use crate::{
    Error, Expr, MAX_DECLARATIONS, MAX_EXPRESSIONS, MAX_STATEMENTS, Program, Statement, Type, UInt,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

fn failure(code: &str, message: impl Into<String>) -> Error {
    Error::new(code, message)
}

fn invariant(what: &str) -> Error {
    failure("program", format!("Stage plan invariant violated: {what}."))
}

/// Legacy identifier rule with `await` and `when` also reserved (C6).
fn identifier_v2(name: &str) -> bool {
    identifier(name) && !matches!(name, "await" | "when")
}

fn names_v2<'a>(values: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>, kind: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    for name in values {
        if !identifier_v2(name) || !seen.insert(name) {
            return Err(failure(
                "duplicate",
                format!("Invalid or duplicate {kind} name {name:?}."),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Full finite validation of a `moriarty-core/2` program.
pub(crate) fn validate_v2(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE_2 || program.semantics != SEMANTICS_2 {
        return Err(failure(
            "profile",
            "Unsupported language or semantics identity.",
        ));
    }
    if !identifier_v2(&program.name) {
        return Err(failure(
            "name",
            "Agreement name must be a non-reserved ASCII identifier of at most 64 bytes.",
        ));
    }
    if program.actions.is_empty() {
        return Err(failure("program", "Program needs at least one action."));
    }
    if program.states.len() + program.assets.len() + program.actions.len() > MAX_DECLARATIONS
        || program.expressions.len() > MAX_EXPRESSIONS
    {
        return Err(failure(
            "bound",
            "Program exceeds finite declaration/expression bounds.",
        ));
    }
    names_v2(
        program
            .states
            .iter()
            .map(|s| s.name.as_str())
            .chain(program.assets.iter().map(|a| a.name.as_str())),
        "declaration",
    )?;
    names_v2(program.actions.iter().map(|a| a.name.as_str()), "action")?;
    let mut identities = BTreeSet::new();
    for asset in &program.assets {
        let id = &asset.identity;
        if id.network.is_empty()
            || id.issuer.is_empty()
            || id.reference.is_empty()
            || id.network.len() > 1024
            || id.issuer.len() > 1024
            || id.reference.len() > 1024
            || id.scale > 38
            || !identities.insert(id)
        {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Asset identities must be complete, unique and use scale 0..38.",
            ));
        }
        if program.assets.iter().any(|other| {
            other.identity.network == id.network
                && other.identity.issuer == id.issuer
                && other.identity.reference == id.reference
                && other.identity.scale != id.scale
        }) {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Same asset identity cannot have conflicting scales.",
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut depths = Vec::with_capacity(program.expressions.len());
    for (i, e) in program.expressions.iter().enumerate() {
        let refs = match e {
            Expr::Binary { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![*lhs, *rhs],
            Expr::Not { value } => vec![*value],
            _ => vec![],
        };
        let mut depth = 0;
        for r in refs {
            if usize::from(r) >= i {
                return Err(failure(
                    "expression",
                    "Expression references must point to earlier nodes; cycles are forbidden.",
                ));
            }
            depth = depth.max(depths[usize::from(r)] + 1);
        }
        if depth > 64 {
            return Err(failure("bound", "Expression depth exceeds 64."));
        }
        depths.push(depth);
    }
    let state_types: BTreeMap<_, _> = program
        .states
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.ty))
        .collect();
    for state in &program.states {
        if state.initial.ty() != state.ty {
            return Err(failure(
                "type",
                format!("Initial state {:?} has wrong type.", state.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    for action in &program.actions {
        if action.inputs.len() > MAX_DECLARATIONS || action.statements.len() > MAX_STATEMENTS {
            return Err(failure(
                "bound",
                "Action exceeds input or statement bounds.",
            ));
        }
        names_v2(action.inputs.iter().map(|i| i.name.as_str()), "input")?;
        let mut env = state_types.clone();
        for input in &action.inputs {
            if env.insert(input.name.clone(), input.ty).is_some()
                || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == input.name)
            {
                return Err(failure("duplicate", "Input cannot shadow a declaration."));
            }
        }
        let mut labels = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut awaits = 0_usize;
        // Inputs, lets and earlier binders: the captures of the next site.
        let mut captured = action.inputs.len();
        for statement in &action.statements {
            match statement {
                Statement::Await {
                    label,
                    binders,
                    guard,
                } => {
                    awaits += 1;
                    if awaits > MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION {
                        return Err(failure("bound", "Action exceeds 16 awaits."));
                    }
                    if binders.len() > MAX_EVENT_BINDERS {
                        return Err(failure("bound", "Await exceeds 16 event binders."));
                    }
                    if captured > MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS {
                        return Err(failure("bound", "Await site exceeds 256 capture slots."));
                    }
                    if !identifier_v2(label) || !labels.insert(label.as_str()) {
                        return Err(failure(
                            "duplicate",
                            format!("Invalid or duplicate await label {label:?}."),
                        ));
                    }
                    for binder in binders {
                        if !identifier_v2(&binder.name)
                            || env.insert(binder.name.clone(), binder.ty).is_some()
                            || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == binder.name)
                        {
                            return Err(failure(
                                "duplicate",
                                "Await binder cannot shadow an existing name.",
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                    if expr_type(program, *guard, &env, 0)? != Type::Bool {
                        return Err(failure("type", "Await guard must have type Bool."));
                    }
                    captured += binders.len();
                }
                Statement::Let { name, value } => {
                    let ty = expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)?;
                    if !identifier_v2(name)
                        || env.insert(name.clone(), ty).is_some()
                        || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == *name)
                    {
                        return Err(failure("duplicate", "let cannot shadow an existing name."));
                    }
                    captured += 1;
                }
                Statement::Requires { predicate } | Statement::Ensures { predicate } => {
                    if expr_type(program, *predicate, &env, 0)? != Type::Bool {
                        return Err(failure("type", "Predicate must have type Bool."));
                    }
                }
                Statement::Next { state, value } => {
                    let expected = state_types
                        .get(state)
                        .ok_or_else(|| failure("name", format!("Unknown state {state:?}.")))?;
                    if expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)? != *expected {
                        return Err(failure("type", "State update has wrong type."));
                    }
                }
                Statement::Emit { name, value } => {
                    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure("name", "Event name must contain 1..1024 bytes."));
                    }
                    expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)?;
                }
                Statement::Transfer {
                    asset,
                    from,
                    to,
                    amount,
                }
                | Statement::Fee {
                    asset,
                    from,
                    to,
                    amount,
                } => {
                    validate_asset(program, asset)?;
                    if from.is_empty() || to.is_empty() || from.len() > 1024 || to.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure("account", "Account identities cannot be empty."));
                    }
                    require_uint(program, *amount, &env)?;
                }
                Statement::Liability {
                    name,
                    asset,
                    debtor,
                    creditor,
                    amount,
                } => {
                    validate_asset(program, asset)?;
                    if name.is_empty()
                        || debtor.is_empty()
                        || creditor.is_empty()
                        || name.len() > 1024
                        || debtor.len() > 1024
                        || creditor.len() > 1024
                    {
                        return Err(failure(
                            "liability",
                            "Liability identities cannot be empty.",
                        ));
                    }
                    require_uint(program, *amount, &env)?;
                }
                Statement::Discharge { name, amount } => {
                    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure(
                            "liability",
                            "Liability name must contain 1..1024 bytes.",
                        ));
                    }
                    require_uint(program, *amount, &env)?;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    validate_liability_reads(program)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Independently re-derives each action's sites and capture layouts and
/// requires the Sol-built plan to equal them, then checks the A3 predicates
/// explicitly. Runs before costing, so cost vectors and hash must be empty.
pub(crate) fn plan_invariants(program: &Program, plan: &StagePlan) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if plan.format != STAGE_PLAN_FORMAT {
        return Err(invariant("format"));
    }
    if !plan.program_hash.is_empty() {
        return Err(invariant("program hash filled before costing"));
    }
    if plan.actions.len() != program.actions.len() {
        return Err(invariant("action count"));
    }
    let state_names: BTreeSet<_> = program.states.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();
    for (action, ap) in program.actions.iter().zip(&plan.actions) {
        if ap.action != action.name || usize::from(ap.statement_count) != action.statements.len() {
            return Err(invariant("action identity"));
        }
        if !ap.segment_cost.is_empty()
            || !ap.committed_before.is_empty()
            || ap.plan_total != UInt(0)
        {
            return Err(invariant("costs filled before costing"));
        }
        // Independent derivation in declaration and statement order.
        let mut types: BTreeMap<_, _> = program
            .states
            .iter()
            .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.ty))
            .collect();
        let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(action.inputs.len());
        for (index, input) in action.inputs.iter().enumerate() {
            types.insert(input.name.clone(), input.ty);
            slots.push(CaptureSlot {
                name: input.name.clone(),
                ty: input.ty,
                origin: Origin::Input,
                ordinal: u16::try_from(index).map_err(|_| invariant("input ordinal"))?,
            });
        }
        let mut expected = Vec::new();
        for (index, statement) in action.statements.iter().enumerate() {
            let ordinal = u16::try_from(index).map_err(|_| invariant("statement ordinal"))?;
            match statement {
                Statement::Let { name, value } => {
                    let ty = expr_type(program, *value, &types, 0)?;
                    types.insert(name.clone(), ty);
                    slots.push(CaptureSlot {
                        name: name.clone(),
                        ty,
                        origin: Origin::Let,
                        ordinal,
                    });
                }
                Statement::Await { label, binders, .. } => {
                    expected.push(AwaitSite {
                        site: u16::try_from(expected.len() + 1).map_err(|_| invariant("site"))?,
                        ordinal,
                        label: label.clone(),
                        binders: binders.iter().map(StageBinder::from).collect(),
                        captures: slots.clone(),
                    });
                    for binder in binders {
                        types.insert(binder.name.clone(), binder.ty);
                        slots.push(CaptureSlot {
                            name: binder.name.clone(),
                            ty: binder.ty,
                            origin: Origin::Event,
                            ordinal,
                        });
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        if ap.sites != expected {
            return Err(invariant("sites differ from source"));
        }
        // Explicit A3 predicates, stated separately from the derivation.
        if ap.sites.len() > MAX_AWAITS_PER_ACTION {
            return Err(failure("bound", "Action exceeds 16 awaits."));
        }
        let mut previous: Option<&AwaitSite> = None;
        for (index, site) in ap.sites.iter().enumerate() {
            if usize::from(site.site) != index + 1 {
                return Err(invariant("sites are not numbered 1..N"));
            }
            if previous.is_some_and(|p| p.ordinal >= site.ordinal) {
                return Err(invariant("ordinals are not strictly increasing"));
            }
            if site.binders.len() > MAX_EVENT_BINDERS || site.captures.len() > MAX_CAPTURE_SLOTS {
                return Err(failure("bound", "Await site exceeds stage layout bounds."));
            }
            let inputs = action.inputs.len();
            if site.captures.len() < inputs
                || site.captures[..inputs]
                    .iter()
                    .zip(&action.inputs)
                    .enumerate()
                    .any(|(i, (slot, input))| {
                        slot.origin != Origin::Input
                            || slot.name != input.name
                            || slot.ty != input.ty
                            || usize::from(slot.ordinal) != i
                    })
            {
                return Err(invariant("captures do not begin with all inputs"));
            }
            let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
            for slot in &site.captures {
                if state_names.contains(slot.name.as_str())
                    || !seen.insert(slot.name.as_str())
                    || (slot.origin != Origin::Input && slot.ordinal >= site.ordinal)
                {
                    return Err(invariant(
                        "capture names a state, repeats or follows its site",
                    ));
                }
            }
            if let Some(p) = previous
                && !site.captures.starts_with(&p.captures)
            {
                return Err(invariant("captures are not prefix-monotone"));
            }
            previous = Some(site);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Checks the filled cost vectors: N+1 entries, prefix sums, and a total that
/// also equals the per-statement sum plus one entry charge per await.
pub(crate) fn cost_invariants(program: &Program, plan: &StagePlan) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let overflow = || failure("bound", "Stage logical plan exceeds u128.");
    for (action, ap) in program.actions.iter().zip(&plan.actions) {
        let segments = ap.sites.len() + 1;
        if ap.segment_cost.len() != segments || ap.committed_before.len() != segments {
            return Err(invariant("cost vector lengths"));
        }
        let mut running = 0_u128;
        for (cost, before) in ap.segment_cost.iter().zip(&ap.committed_before) {
            if before.0 != running {
                return Err(invariant("committed_before is not a prefix sum"));
            }
            running = running.checked_add(cost.0).ok_or_else(overflow)?;
        }
        if ap.plan_total.0 != running {
            return Err(invariant("plan total"));
        }
        let mut independent = u128::try_from(ap.sites.len()).map_err(|_| overflow())?;
        for statement in &action.statements {
            let cost = super::cost::statement_cost(program, statement)?;
            independent = independent.checked_add(cost.0).ok_or_else(overflow)?;
        }
        if independent != running {
            return Err(invariant("plan total differs from statement costs"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
<END X030>

## X031: crates/mori-core/tests/language.rs
