<BEGIN X031>
use mori_core::*;

const COUNTER: &str = r#"language "moriarty/1";
agreement Counter {
 state count: UInt = 0;
 action increment(amount: UInt) {
   let total = count + amount;
   requires total <= 100;
   next count = total;
   ensures count == total;
   emit "count"(count);
 }
 action double() { next count = count * 2; }
}"#;
fn uint(n: u128) -> Value {
    Value::UInt(UInt(n))
}
#[test]
fn authored_counter_selects_actions_and_preserves_dependencies() {
    let p = parse(COUNTER).unwrap();
    let mut s = Scenario::default();
    s.inputs.insert("amount".into(), uint(7));
    let run = simulate(&p, "increment", &s).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run.post.state["count"], uint(7));
    assert_eq!(run.steps.len(), 5);
    replay(&p, "increment", &s, &run).unwrap();
    s.state = run.post.state;
    s.inputs.clear();
    assert_eq!(
        simulate(&p, "double", &s).unwrap().post.state["count"],
        uint(14)
    );
}
#[test]
fn failed_predicate_leaves_original_scenario_unchanged() {
    let p = parse(COUNTER).unwrap();
    let mut s = Scenario::default();
    s.inputs.insert("amount".into(), uint(101));
    let original = s.clone();
    assert_eq!(
        simulate(&p, "increment", &s).unwrap_err().code,
        "mori::core::requires"
    );
    assert_eq!(s, original);
}

const PAYMENT: &str = r#"language "moriarty/1";
agreement ConditionalPayment {
 asset USD = { network: "preview", issuer: "issuer", reference: "usd", scale: 2 };
 state paid: UInt = 0;
 action settle(amount: UInt, approved: Bool) {
   requires approved and amount > 0;
   let charge = amount + 2;
   transfer(USD, "alice", "bob", amount);
   fee(USD, "alice", "treasury", 2);
   liability("delivery", USD, "bob", "alice", amount);
   next paid = paid + charge;
   ensures paid >= charge;
   emit "settled"(paid);
 }
 action finish(amount: UInt) { discharge("delivery", amount); }
}"#;
fn payment() -> (Program, Scenario) {
    let p = parse(PAYMENT).unwrap();
    let asset = p.assets[0].identity.clone();
    let mut s = Scenario::default();
    s.inputs.insert("amount".into(), uint(20));
    s.inputs.insert("approved".into(), Value::Bool(true));
    s.balances = vec![
        Balance {
            account: "alice".into(),
            asset: asset.clone(),
            amount: UInt(100),
        },
        Balance {
            account: "bob".into(),
            asset: asset.clone(),
            amount: UInt(0),
        },
        Balance {
            account: "treasury".into(),
            asset,
            amount: UInt(0),
        },
    ];
    (p, s)
}
#[test]
fn authored_payment_has_complete_ordered_effects_and_persistent_liability() {
    let (p, s) = payment();
    let run = simulate(&p, "settle", &s).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run.post.state["paid"], uint(22));
    assert_eq!(run.effects.len(), 5);
    assert_eq!(
        run.post
            .balances
            .iter()
            .find(|b| b.account == "alice")
            .unwrap()
            .amount,
        UInt(78)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        run.post.balances.iter().map(|b| b.amount.0).sum::<u128>(),
        100
    );
    assert_eq!(run.post.liabilities[0].amount, UInt(20));
    let mut next = Scenario {
        state: run.post.state,
        balances: run.post.balances,
        liabilities: run.post.liabilities,
        ..Scenario::default()
    };
    next.inputs.insert("amount".into(), uint(7));
    assert_eq!(
        simulate(&p, "finish", &next).unwrap().post.liabilities[0].amount,
        UInt(13)
    );
}
#[test]
fn late_fee_failure_rolls_back_every_effect() {
    let (p, mut s) = payment();
    s.balances[0].amount = UInt(21);
    let before = s.clone();
    let e = simulate(&p, "settle", &s).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(e.code, "mori::core::balance");
    assert_eq!(e.step, Some(3));
    assert_eq!(s, before);
}
#[test]
fn replay_identifies_first_step_divergence_and_missing_effects() {
    let (p, s) = payment();
    let run = simulate(&p, "settle", &s).unwrap();
    let mut wrong = run.clone();
    wrong.steps[2].effects.clear();
    assert_eq!(replay(&p, "settle", &s, &wrong).unwrap_err().step, Some(2));
    let mut wrong = run;
    wrong.effects.pop();
    assert_eq!(
        replay(&p, "settle", &s, &wrong).unwrap_err().code,
        "mori::core::replay"
    );
}
#[test]
fn exact_input_and_balance_schemas_are_required() {
    let (p, mut s) = payment();
    s.inputs.remove("amount");
    assert_eq!(
        simulate(&p, "settle", &s).unwrap_err().code,
        "mori::core::input"
    );
    let (_, mut s) = payment();
    s.inputs.insert("unexpected".into(), uint(1));
    assert_eq!(
        simulate(&p, "settle", &s).unwrap_err().code,
        "mori::core::input"
    );
    let (_, mut s) = payment();
    s.inputs.insert("amount".into(), Value::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(
        simulate(&p, "settle", &s).unwrap_err().code,
        "mori::core::input"
    );
    let (_, mut s) = payment();
    s.balances.pop();

<BEGIN X034>
//! Lexer for `moriarty-beta/1` source.
//!
//! Turns source text into [`Tokens`] in a single pass.
//!
//! Lexing stops at the first error. Whitespace is skipped; comments are kept
//! separately for the formatter and do not count toward [`MAX_TOKENS`].

mod diagnostics;
mod number;
mod scan;
mod string;
mod token;

#[cfg(test)]
mod proptests;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use mori_diagnostics::MoriDiagnostic;
use mori_span::Span;
use soa_rs::Soa;

use crate::number::NumberError;
use crate::string::StringErrorKind;

pub use crate::token::{Comment, Token, TokenIdx, TokenKind, Tokens};

/// Largest accepted source file, in bytes.
pub const MAX_SOURCE_BYTES: usize = 65_536;
/// Most tokens in one file, including the end-of-file token.
pub const MAX_TOKENS: usize = 8_192;
/// Longest identifier or keyword, in bytes.
pub const MAX_IDENT_BYTES: usize = 64;
/// Longest decoded string, in UTF-8 bytes.
pub const MAX_STRING_BYTES: usize = 1_024;

/// The text of a string token, with escapes decoded.
///
/// `raw` must be the full text of a [`TokenKind::String`] token, quotes
/// included, as produced by [`lex`].
pub fn decode_string(raw: &str) -> String {
    let mut text = String::with_capacity(raw.len());
    string::decode_with(raw, |c| text.push(c)).expect("lexed strings are valid");
    text
}

/// Splits `source` into tokens and comments, or reports the first error.
pub fn lex(source: &str) -> Result<Tokens, MoriDiagnostic> {
    if source.len() > MAX_SOURCE_BYTES {
        return Err(diagnostics::source_too_large(source.len()));
    }
    Lexer::new(source).run(false)
}

/// Identify a leading profile token without requiring the remaining source to
/// lex successfully. Inspect only a bounded prefix; full parsing retains all
/// source and token limits.
pub fn first_token_text(source: &str) -> Result<&str, MoriDiagnostic> {
    let end = source.floor_char_boundary(source.len().min(MAX_SOURCE_BYTES));
    let prefix = &source[..end];
    let tokens = Lexer::new(prefix).run(true)?;
    Ok(tokens.span(TokenIdx::new(0), prefix).source_text(prefix))
}

struct Lexer<'src> {
    source: &'src str,
    bytes: &'src [u8],
    pos: usize,
    tokens: Soa<Token>,
    comments: Soa<Comment>,
}

impl<'src> Lexer<'src> {
    fn new(source: &'src str) -> Self {
        Self {
            source,
            bytes: source.as_bytes(),
            pos: 0,
            // Roughly one token per eight bytes, as in Zig.
            tokens: Soa::with_capacity(source.len() / 8 + 1),
            comments: Soa::new(),
        }
    }

    fn run(mut self, first_only: bool) -> Result<Tokens, MoriDiagnostic> {
        while let Some(&b) = self.bytes.get(self.pos) {
            let start = self.pos;
            match b {
                b' ' | b'\t' | b'\r' | b'\n' => self.pos += 1,
                b'/' if self.peek(1) == Some(b'/') => self.line_comment(start),
                b'/' if self.peek(1) == Some(b'*') => self.block_comment(start)?,
                b'"' => self.string(start)?,
                b'0'..=b'9' => self.number(start)?,
                b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' => self.word(start)?,
                _ => match TokenKind::punctuation(b) {
                    Some(kind) => self.push(kind, start, start + 1)?,
                    None => return Err(self.unexpected_character(start)),
                },
            }
            if first_only && !self.tokens.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
        }
        // The end-of-file token is always pushed: the bound reserves room for it.
        self.tokens.push(Token {
            kind: TokenKind::Eof,
            start: offset(self.pos),
        });
        Ok(Tokens {
            tokens: self.tokens,
            comments: self.comments,
        })
    }

    fn peek(&self, ahead: usize) -> Option<u8> {
        self.bytes.get(self.pos + ahead).copied()
    }

    /// Records a token ending at `end` and moves past it.
    fn push(&mut self, kind: TokenKind, start: usize, end: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        if self.tokens.len() >= MAX_TOKENS - 1 {
            return Err(diagnostics::too_many_tokens(span(start, end)));
        }
        self.tokens.push(Token {
            kind,
            start: offset(start),
        });
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn push_comment(&mut self, start: usize, end: usize) {
        self.comments.push(Comment {
            start: offset(start),
            end: offset(end),
        });
        self.pos = end;
    }

    /// `//` up to, but not including, the next line break.
    fn line_comment(&mut self, start: usize) {
        let end = self.bytes[start..]
            .iter()
            .position(|&b| b == b'\r' || b == b'\n')
            .map_or(self.bytes.len(), |len| start + len);
        self.push_comment(start, end);
    }

    /// `/*` through the first `*/`. Block comments do not nest.
    fn block_comment(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let body = start + 2;
        let Some(len) = self.source[body..].find("*/") else {
            return Err(diagnostics::unterminated_block_comment(span(start, body)));
        };
        self.push_comment(start, body + len + 2);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn string(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let Some(end) = scan::string_end(self.bytes, start) else {
            return Err(diagnostics::unterminated_string(span(start, start + 1)));
        };
        let raw = &self.source[start..end];
        let mut decoded_len = 0;
        if let Err(error) = string::decode_with(raw, |c| decoded_len += c.len_utf8()) {
            let at = span(start + error.start, start + error.end);
            return Err(match error.kind {
                StringErrorKind::ControlCharacter('\r' | '\n') => {
                    diagnostics::string_line_break(at)
                }
                StringErrorKind::ControlCharacter(c) => {
                    diagnostics::string_control_character(at, c)
                }
                StringErrorKind::InvalidEscape => {
                    diagnostics::invalid_escape(at, at.source_text(self.source))
                }
                StringErrorKind::InvalidUnicodeEscape => diagnostics::invalid_unicode_escape(at),
                StringErrorKind::LoneSurrogate => diagnostics::lone_surrogate(at),
            });
        }
        if decoded_len > MAX_STRING_BYTES {
            return Err(diagnostics::string_too_long(span(start, end), decoded_len));
        }
        self.push(TokenKind::String, start, end)
    }

    fn number(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let end = scan::number_end(self.bytes, start);
        let raw = &self.source[start..end];
        if let Err(error) = number::validate(raw) {
            return Err(match error {
                NumberError::LeadingZero => diagnostics::number_leading_zero(
                    span(start, end),
                    &number::without_leading_zeros(raw),
                ),
                NumberError::MisplacedUnderscore { at } => {
                    diagnostics::number_misplaced_underscore(span(start + at, start + at + 1))
                }
                NumberError::MissingFraction => {
                    diagnostics::number_missing_fraction(span(end - 1, end))
                }
                NumberError::ExtraDot { at } => {
                    diagnostics::number_extra_dot(span(start + at, start + at + 1))
                }
            });
        }
        self.push(TokenKind::Number, start, end)
    }

    /// An identifier, or a keyword when the text matches one.
    fn word(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let end = scan::word_end(self.bytes, start);
        if end - start > MAX_IDENT_BYTES {
            return Err(diagnostics::identifier_too_long(span(start, end)));
        }
        let kind = TokenKind::keyword(&self.source[start..end]).unwrap_or(TokenKind::Ident);
        self.push(kind, start, end)
    }

    fn unexpected_character(&self, start: usize) -> MoriDiagnostic {
        let c = self.source[start..]
            .chars()
            .next()
            .expect("a character remains at the current position");
        let at = span(start, start + c.len_utf8());
        match c {
            '/' => diagnostics::division(at),
            '“' | '”' | '‘' | '’' => diagnostics::curly_quote(at),
            '\'' => diagnostics::single_quote(at),
            '_' => diagnostics::leading_underscore(at),
            c if !c.is_ascii() => diagnostics::non_ascii(at, c),
            c => diagnostics::unexpected_character(at, c),
        }
    }
}

/// Converts a byte index to an offset. Sources fit in `u32` after the bound check.
fn offset(index: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(index).expect("source offsets fit in u32")
}

fn span(start: usize, end: usize) -> Span {
    Span::new(offset(start), offset(end))
}

<BEGIN X041>
//! Parser for `moriarty-beta/1` source.
//!
//! [`parse`] lexes and parses a file into an [`Ast`], stopping at the first
//! error. It checks syntax and syntactic bounds only; names, types and values
//! are checked by later phases.

mod diagnostics;
mod parser;

#[cfg(test)]
mod proptests;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use mori_ast::Ast;
use mori_diagnostics::MoriDiagnostic;

/// The only profile this parser accepts.
pub const PROFILE: &str = "moriarty-beta/1";
/// Deepest nesting of expressions and types.
pub const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 64;
/// Most fields in one record or call, and most type arguments.
pub const MAX_FIELDS: usize = 64;
/// Most declarations and actions in one agreement.
pub const MAX_ITEMS: usize = 256;

/// Lexes and parses `source`, or reports the first error.
pub fn parse(source: &str) -> Result<Ast<'_>, MoriDiagnostic> {
    let tokens = mori_lexer::lex(source)?;
    let (nodes, extra) = parser::Parser::new(source, &tokens).run()?;
    Ok(Ast {
        source,
        tokens,
        nodes,
        extra,
    })
}

<BEGIN X042>
//! Recursive-descent parser over the token array.
//!
//! The grammar, with `WORD` meaning an identifier or keyword:
//!
//! ```text
//! file      = "profile" STRING ";" "agreement" IDENT "{" { item } "}" EOF ;
//! item      = KIND IDENT [ ":" type ] "=" expr ";"
//!           | "action" IDENT "uses" IDENT ";" ;
//! type      = WORD [ "<" type { "," type } ">" ] ;
//! expr      = term { ( "+" | "-" ) term } ;
//! term      = primary { "*" primary } ;
//! primary   = STRING | NUMBER [ IDENT ] | "true" | "false" | "None"
//!           | "SuccessOnly" | "(" expr ")" | "[" [ expr { "," expr } [ "," ] ] "]"
//!           | "{" fields "}" | WORD { "." WORD } [ "(" fields ")" ] ;
//! fields    = [ WORD ":" expr { "," WORD ":" expr } [ "," ] ] ;
//! ```
//!
//! A dotted name must be a call. A number directly followed by an identifier
//! is a quantity; a decimal number must have one.

use mori_ast::{Node, NodeTag};
use mori_diagnostics::MoriDiagnostic;
use mori_lexer::{TokenIdx, TokenKind, Tokens};
use mori_span::Span;
use soa_rs::Soa;

use crate::diagnostics::{self, Context, Expected, Frame};
use crate::{MAX_DEPTH, MAX_FIELDS, MAX_ITEMS, PROFILE};

type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, MoriDiagnostic>;

pub struct Parser<'a> {
    source: &'a str,
    tokens: &'a Tokens,
    pos: usize,
    nodes: Soa<Node>,
    extra: Vec<u16>,
    /// Children of lists still being parsed. Each list drains its own top.
    scratch: Vec<u16>,
    /// What is being parsed, innermost last, for error messages.
    frames: Vec<Frame>,
}

impl<'a> Parser<'a> {
    pub fn new(source: &'a str, tokens: &'a Tokens) -> Self {
        Self {
            source,
            tokens,
            pos: 0,
            nodes: Soa::with_capacity(tokens.len()),
            extra: Vec::new(),
            scratch: Vec::new(),
            frames: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn run(mut self) -> Result<(Soa<Node>, Vec<u16>)> {
        // Reserve node 0 for the root; it is filled in once the items are known.
        self.push(NodeTag::Agreement, TokenIdx::new(0), 0, 0);

        let profile = self.current();
        self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Profile, profile));
        self.expect(TokenKind::KwProfile, "mori::syntax::missing_profile")?;
        self.profile_string()?;
        self.expect(TokenKind::Semicolon, "mori::syntax::missing_semicolon")?;
        self.frames.pop();

        let agreement = self.current();
        self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Agreement, agreement));
        self.expect(TokenKind::KwAgreement, "mori::syntax::missing_agreement")?;
        let name = self.name()?;
        self.expect(TokenKind::LBrace, "mori::syntax::missing_opening_brace")?;
        self.frames.pop();

        self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Body, name));
        let start = self.scratch.len();
        while self.eat(TokenKind::RBrace).is_none() {
            if self.scratch.len() - start >= MAX_ITEMS {
                return Err(diagnostics::too_many_items(self.current_span()));
            }
            let item = self.item()?;
            self.scratch.push(item);
        }
        let (lhs, rhs) = self.finish_list(start);
        self.frames.pop();

        self.nodes.main_token_mut()[0] = name;
        self.nodes.lhs_mut()[0] = lhs;
        self.nodes.rhs_mut()[0] = rhs;

        if self.peek() != TokenKind::Eof {
            return Err(diagnostics::trailing_input(self.current_span()));
        }
        Ok((self.nodes, self.extra))
    }

    fn profile_string(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.peek() != TokenKind::String {
            return Err(
                self.unexpected("mori::syntax::expected_profile", &[Expected::ProfileString])
            );
        }
        let token = self.bump();
        let span = self.span(token);
        let profile = mori_lexer::decode_string(span.source_text(self.source));
        if profile != PROFILE {
            return Err(diagnostics::wrong_profile(span, &profile));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn item(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let kind = self.peek();
        if kind == TokenKind::KwAction {
            self.action()
        } else if kind.is_declaration_kind() {
            self.declaration()
        } else {
            let span = self.current_span();
            Err(match kind {
                TokenKind::Eof => {
                    let last = self.span(TokenIdx::new(self.pos - 1));
                    let span = Span::empty(last.end);
                    let name = self.span(self.agreement_name());
                    diagnostics::unclosed_agreement(span, name, name.source_text(self.source))
                }
                TokenKind::Ident => diagnostics::unknown_item(
                    span,
                    Some(span.source_text(self.source)),
                    self.source,
                ),
                _ => diagnostics::unknown_item(span, None, self.source),
            })
        }
    }

    /// `KIND NAME [: TYPE] = VALUE ;`
    fn declaration(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let kind = self.bump();
        self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Declaration, kind));
        self.name()?;
        let ty = match self.eat(TokenKind::Colon) {
            Some(_) => self.ty(1)?,
            None => 0,
        };
        self.expect(TokenKind::Eq, "mori::syntax::missing_equals")?;
        let value = self.expression(1, 0)?;
        self.expect(TokenKind::Semicolon, "mori::syntax::missing_semicolon")?;
        self.frames.pop();
        Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Declaration, kind, ty, value))
    }

    /// `action NAME uses INTENT ;`
    fn action(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let action = self.bump();
        self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Action, action));
        self.name()?;
        self.expect(TokenKind::KwUses, "mori::syntax::missing_uses")?;
        self.name()?;
        self.expect(TokenKind::Semicolon, "mori::syntax::missing_semicolon")?;
        self.frames.pop();
        Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Action, action, 0, 0))
    }

    /// A declaration, action or agreement name: an identifier, not a keyword.
    fn name(&mut self) -> Result<TokenIdx> {
        match self.peek() {
            TokenKind::Ident => Ok(self.bump()),
            kind if kind.is_keyword() => {
                let span = self.current_span();
                Err(diagnostics::keyword_as_name(
                    span,
                    span.source_text(self.source),
                    self.source,
                ))
            }
            _ => Err(self.unexpected("mori::syntax::expected_name", &[Expected::Name])),
        }
    }

    /// `WORD [< TYPE, ... >]`
    fn ty(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<u16> {
        self.check_depth(depth)?;
        if !self.peek().is_word() {
            return Err(self.unexpected("mori::syntax::expected_type", &[Expected::Type]));
        }
        let name = self.bump();
        let start = self.scratch.len();
        if let Some(open) = self.eat(TokenKind::Lt) {
            self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Type, name));
            loop {
                if self.scratch.len() - start >= MAX_FIELDS {
                    return Err(diagnostics::too_many_type_arguments(self.span(open)));
                }
                let arg = self.ty(depth + 1)?;
                self.scratch.push(arg);
                if self.eat(TokenKind::Comma).is_none() {
                    break;
                }
            }
            self.expect(TokenKind::Gt, "mori::syntax::unclosed_type_arguments")?;
            self.frames.pop();
        }
        let (lhs, rhs) = self.finish_list(start);
        Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Type, name, lhs, rhs))
    }

    /// Binary operators by precedence climbing. All operators associate left.
    fn expression(&mut self, depth: usize, min_precedence: u8) -> Result<u16> {
        self.check_depth(depth)?;
        let mut lhs = self.primary(depth)?;
        loop {
            let (tag, precedence) = match self.peek() {
                TokenKind::Star => (NodeTag::Mul, 2),
                TokenKind::Plus => (NodeTag::Add, 1),
                TokenKind::Minus => (NodeTag::Sub, 1),
                _ => break,
            };
            if precedence < min_precedence {
                break;
            }
            let operator = self.bump();
            let rhs = self.expression(depth + 1, precedence + 1)?;
            lhs = self.push(tag, operator, lhs, rhs);
        }
        Ok(lhs)
    }

    fn primary(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<u16> {
        let kind = self.peek();
        match kind {
            TokenKind::String => Ok(self.leaf(NodeTag::String)),
            TokenKind::Number => self.number(),
            TokenKind::KwTrue | TokenKind::KwFalse => Ok(self.leaf(NodeTag::Bool)),
            TokenKind::KwNone | TokenKind::KwSuccessOnly => Ok(self.leaf(NodeTag::Tag)),
            TokenKind::LParen => {
                let open = self.bump();
                self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Paren, open));
                let inner = self.expression(depth + 1, 0)?;
                self.expect(TokenKind::RParen, "mori::syntax::unclosed_parenthesis")?;
                self.frames.pop();
                Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Paren, open, inner, 0))
            }
            TokenKind::LBracket => self.array(depth),
            TokenKind::LBrace => {
                let open = self.bump();
                self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Record, open));
                let (lhs, rhs) = self.fields(TokenKind::RBrace, depth)?;
                self.frames.pop();
                Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Record, open, lhs, rhs))
            }
            _ if kind.is_word() => self.name_or_call(depth),
            _ => Err(self.unexpected("mori::syntax::expected_value", &[Expected::Expression])),
        }
    }

    /// A number, or a quantity when an asset name follows.
    fn number(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let number = self.bump();
        let number_span = self.span(number);
        if self.peek() == TokenKind::Ident {
            let asset = self.bump();
            let asset_span = self.span(asset);
            if asset_span.start == number_span.end {
                return Err(diagnostics::quantity_separator(
                    number_span,
                    asset_span,
                    self.source,
                ));
            }
            return Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Quantity, number, 0, 0));
        }
        if number_span.source_text(self.source).contains('.') {
            return Err(diagnostics::decimal_without_asset(number_span, self.source));
        }
        Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Number, number, 0, 0))
    }

    /// `[ ITEM, ... ]` with an optional trailing comma.
    fn array(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<u16> {
        let open = self.bump();
        self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Array, open));
        let start = self.scratch.len();
        if self.eat(TokenKind::RBracket).is_none() {
            loop {
                let item = self.expression(depth + 1, 0)?;
                self.scratch.push(item);
                if self.eat(TokenKind::RBracket).is_some() {
                    break;
                }
                if self.starts_expression() {
                    return Err(self.missing_comma("items"));
                }
                self.expect_one_of(
                    &[TokenKind::Comma, TokenKind::RBracket],
                    "mori::syntax::unclosed_list",
                )?;
                if self.eat(TokenKind::RBracket).is_some() {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        let (lhs, rhs) = self.finish_list(start);
        self.frames.pop();
        Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Array, open, lhs, rhs))
    }

    /// A reference, or a call when `(` follows. Dotted names must be calls.
    fn name_or_call(&mut self, depth: usize) -> Result<u16> {
        let first = self.bump();
        let mut last = first;
        while self.eat(TokenKind::Dot).is_some() {
            if !self.peek().is_word() {
                self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::CallName, first));
                return Err(self.unexpected(
                    "mori::syntax::incomplete_call_name",
                    &[Expected::NameSegment],
                ));
            }
            last = self.bump();
        }
        if self.eat(TokenKind::LParen).is_some() {
            self.frames.push(Frame::new(Context::Call, first));
            let (lhs, rhs) = self.fields(TokenKind::RParen, depth)?;
            self.frames.pop();
            return Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Call, first, lhs, rhs));
        }
        if last != first {
            let span = Span::new(self.span(first).start, self.span(last).end);
            return Err(diagnostics::dotted_reference(
                span,
                span.source_text(self.source),
                self.source,
            ));
        }
        Ok(self.push(NodeTag::Reference, first, 0, 0))
    }

    /// `KEY: VALUE, ...` up to `close`, with an optional trailing comma.
    fn fields(&mut self, close: TokenKind, depth: usize) -> Result<(u16, u16)> {
        let start = self.scratch.len();
        if self.eat(close).is_none() {
            loop {
                if self.scratch.len() - start >= MAX_FIELDS {
                    return Err(diagnostics::too_many_fields(self.current_span()));
                }
                if !self.peek().is_word() {
                    return Err(self
                        .unexpected("mori::syntax::expected_field_name", &[Expected::FieldName]));
                }
                let key = self.bump();
                self.check_duplicate_field(start, key)?;
                self.expect(TokenKind::Colon, "mori::syntax::missing_colon")?;
                let value = self.expression(depth + 1, 0)?;
                let field = self.push(NodeTag::Field, key, value, 0);
                self.scratch.push(field);
                if self.eat(close).is_some() {
                    break;
                }
                if self.peek().is_word() && self.peek_at(1) == TokenKind::Colon {
                    let between = match close {
                        TokenKind::RBrace => "fields",
                        _ => "arguments",
                    };
                    return Err(self.missing_comma(between));
                }
                let unclosed = match close {
                    TokenKind::RBrace => "mori::syntax::unclosed_record",
                    _ => "mori::syntax::unclosed_call",
                };
                self.expect_one_of(&[TokenKind::Comma, close], unclosed)?;
                if self.eat(close).is_some() {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(self.finish_list(start))
    }

    fn check_duplicate_field(&self, start: usize, key: TokenIdx) -> Result<()> {
        let key_span = self.span(key);
        let text = key_span.source_text(self.source);
        let main_tokens = self.nodes.main_token();
        for &field in &self.scratch[start..] {
            let earlier = self.span(main_tokens[usize::from(field)]);
            if earlier.source_text(self.source) == text {
                return Err(diagnostics::duplicate_field(key_span, earlier, text));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Whether the current token can begin an expression, so a list item
    /// was probably meant to follow.
    fn starts_expression(&self) -> bool {
        let kind = self.peek();
        kind.is_word()
            || matches!(
                kind,
                TokenKind::String
                    | TokenKind::Number
                    | TokenKind::LParen
                    | TokenKind::LBracket
                    | TokenKind::LBrace
            )
    }

    /// Another item follows without a separating comma.
    fn missing_comma(&self, between: &str) -> MoriDiagnostic {
        let previous = self.span(TokenIdx::new(self.pos - 1));
        diagnostics::missing_comma(Span::empty(previous.end), between, self.source)
    }

    fn check_depth(&self, depth: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if depth > MAX_DEPTH {
            return Err(diagnostics::too_deep(self.current_span()));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The agreement name, recorded on the body frame.
    fn agreement_name(&self) -> TokenIdx {
        self.frames
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find(|frame| frame.context == Context::Body)
            .expect("items are parsed inside the agreement body")
            .start
    }

    // Token access

    fn current(&self) -> TokenIdx {
        TokenIdx::new(self.pos)
    }

    fn peek(&self) -> TokenKind {
        self.tokens.kind(self.current())
    }

    /// The kind `ahead` tokens after the current one, or end of file.
    fn peek_at(&self, ahead: usize) -> TokenKind {
        let index = (self.pos + ahead).min(self.tokens.len() - 1);
        self.tokens.kind(TokenIdx::new(index))
    }

    fn span(&self, token: TokenIdx) -> Span {
        self.tokens.span(token, self.source)
    }

    fn current_span(&self) -> Span {
        self.span(self.current())
    }

    /// Consumes the current token. The end-of-file token is never consumed.
    fn bump(&mut self) -> TokenIdx {
        let token = self.current();
        debug_assert_ne!(self.peek(), TokenKind::Eof);
        self.pos += 1;
        token
    }

    fn eat(&mut self, kind: TokenKind) -> Option<TokenIdx> {
        (self.peek() == kind).then(|| self.bump())
    }

    /// Consumes `kind`, or reports `code`.
    fn expect(&mut self, kind: TokenKind, code: &'static str) -> Result<TokenIdx> {
        self.expect_one_of(&[kind], code)
    }

    /// Consumes `expected[0]`, or reports `code`. The other kinds only
    /// describe what else was valid here.
    fn expect_one_of(&mut self, expected: &[TokenKind], code: &'static str) -> Result<TokenIdx> {
        match self.eat(expected[0]) {
            Some(token) => Ok(token),
            None => {
                let expected: Vec<Expected> =
                    expected.iter().map(|&k| Expected::Token(k)).collect();
                Err(self.unexpected(code, &expected))
            }
        }
    }

    fn unexpected(&self, code: &'static str, expected: &[Expected]) -> MoriDiagnostic {
        let found = self.current();
        let previous_end = self
            .pos
            .checked_sub(1)
            .map(|previous| self.span(TokenIdx::new(previous)).end);
        diagnostics::unexpected(diagnostics::Unexpected {
            code,
            source: self.source,
            tokens: self.tokens,
            found,
            previous_end,
            expected,
            frames: &self.frames,
        })
    }

    // Node building

    fn push(&mut self, tag: NodeTag, main_token: TokenIdx, lhs: u16, rhs: u16) -> u16 {
        let index = u16::try_from(self.nodes.len()).expect("nodes never outnumber tokens");
        self.nodes.push(Node {
            tag,
            main_token,
            lhs,
            rhs,
        });
        index
    }

    fn leaf(&mut self, tag: NodeTag) -> u16 {
        let token = self.bump();
        self.push(tag, token, 0, 0)
    }

    /// Moves the scratch entries above `start` into `extra`, returning their range.
    fn finish_list(&mut self, start: usize) -> (u16, u16) {
        let from = self.extra.len();
        self.extra.extend(self.scratch.drain(start..));
        let to = self.extra.len();
        (extra_index(from), extra_index(to))
    }
}

fn extra_index(index: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::try_from(index).expect("extra entries never outnumber nodes")
}
<END X042>

//! Curated public source capabilities, with this binary's actual Cargo features.
//! This query does not inspect files, targets, installations or runtime evidence.
use std::process::ExitCode;

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::shell::Shell;

#[derive(Debug, clap::Args)]
pub struct Args {
    /// Print JSON (the only output format)
    #[arg(long)]
    pub json: bool,
}

// Inspection basis for the curated consumer notes, not a binary/build identity.
// Update this catalogue when public routing or editor implementations change.
const SOURCE_REVISION: &str = "e4d7a2b5709caa18a94f5256d03a0302364b8235";

fn profile(
    id: &str,
    source: &str,
    semantics: Option<&str>,
    parser: &str,
    header_keyword: &str,
    types: &[&str],
) -> Value {
    json!({
        "id": id, "sourceProfile": source,
        "sourceHeader": format!("{header_keyword} \"{source}\";"),
        "semanticsProfile": semantics, "parser": parser,
        "implementation": "source-present",
        "grammar": {
            "coverage": "profile-selection-summary-not-grammar-completion",
            "types": types, "declarations": [], "statements": [],
            "expressions": [], "unsupported": [], "bounds": {},
            "notes": ["Grammar is not enumerated here; use the actual parser/checker for admission."]
        },
        "qualification": "source-description-only",
        "limitations": ["Parser/checker support does not imply compiler or target qualification."]
    })
}

/// Metadata only. The profile tuple is (input, semantics, output); an optional
/// build requirement carries its actual cfg value, not a runtime probe.
fn consumer(
    id: &str,
    entrypoint: &str,
    profiles: (Option<&str>, Option<&str>, Option<&str>),
    build: Option<(&str, bool)>,
    status: (&str, &str),
    limitations: &[&str],
    source_refs: &[&str],
) -> Value {
    let requirements: Vec<_> = build.iter().map(|(name, _)| *name).collect();
    json!({
        "id": id, "entrypoint": entrypoint,
        "inputProfile": profiles.0, "semanticsProfile": profiles.1,
        "outputProfile": profiles.2, "requiresBuildFeatures": requirements,
        "implementation": status.0,
        "availableInBuild": status.0 == "source-present" && build.is_none_or(|(_, enabled)| enabled),
        "qualification": status.1, "limitations": limitations, "sourceRefs": source_refs
    })
}

pub fn run(args: Args, _shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    use mori_core::stage::{LANGUAGE_2, SEMANTICS_2};
    use mori_core::{LANGUAGE, SEMANTICS};

    // JSON is the sole format; the flag is an explicit client spelling.
    let _ = args.json;
    let native = cfg!(feature = "native");
    let source6 = cfg!(feature = "source6-expansion");
    let disjoint = cfg!(feature = "core2-disjoint-draft");
    let report = json!({
        "format": "moriarty-cli-capabilities/1",
        "producer": {
            "implementation": "rust-workspace-cli", "packageVersion": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
            "binarySourceRevision": null, "responseKind": "command-self-report",
            "buildFeatures": {"native": native, "source6-expansion": source6, "core2-disjoint-draft": disjoint}
        },
        "catalogue": {
            "sourceRevision": SOURCE_REVISION, "coverage": "selected-public-profile-consumers",
            "basis": "source-inspection", "runtimeEvidence": "not-included",
            "note": "Curated consumer descriptions use this inspection basis, not an inferred binary revision. Linked profile constants and cfg flags come from the build. Routing/editor changes require a catalogue update."
        },
        "profiles": [
            profile("rust-core1", LANGUAGE, Some(SEMANTICS), "mori_core::parse", "language", &["UInt", "Bool"]),
            profile("rust-core2", LANGUAGE_2, Some(SEMANTICS_2), "mori_core::stage::load", "language", &["UInt", "Bool"]),
            profile("rust-beta-frontend", mori_parser::PROFILE, None, "mori_parser::parse then mori_checker::check", "profile", &[])
        ],
        "consumers": [
            consumer("core1-check", "check FILE --json", (Some(LANGUAGE), Some(SEMANTICS), None), None,
                ("source-present", "source-check"), &["No compilation or target qualification."], &["crates/mori/src/commands/check.rs"]),
            consumer("core2-check", "check FILE --json", (Some(LANGUAGE_2), Some(SEMANTICS_2), None), None,
                ("source-present", "source-check"), &["Uses staged admission and planning."], &["crates/mori/src/commands/check.rs"]),
            consumer("beta-check", "check FILE --json", (Some(mori_parser::PROFILE), None, None), None,
                ("source-present", "frontend-check-only"), &["Named-action admission is determined by the checker; no Core semantics are inferred."], &["crates/mori/src/commands/check.rs"]),
            consumer("core1-reference", "simulate FILE --action NAME --scenario FILE", (Some(LANGUAGE), Some(SEMANTICS), None), None,
                ("source-present", "local-reference-execution"), &["--trace is a separate native-feature consumer."], &["crates/mori/src/commands/simulate.rs"]),

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::time::Instant;

use mori_diagnostics::{MoriDiagnostic, NamedSource};

use crate::json::CheckReport;
use crate::shell::Shell;

use super::check_source::{self, SourceCheckConsumer};

#[derive(Debug, clap::Args)]
pub struct Args {
    /// Source file
    pub file: PathBuf,

    /// Print the result as JSON
    #[arg(long)]
    pub json: bool,
}

/// Checks syntax, names, values, types, declarations, calls and intents.
pub fn run(args: Args, shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    let name = args.file.display().to_string();
    let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;

    if !args.json {
        shell.status("Checking", &name);
    }
    let started = Instant::now();
    let outcome = check_source::dispatch(
        &source,
        CliConsumer {
            name: &name,
            source: &source,
            json: args.json,
            shell,
        },
    )?;
    if outcome.beta {
        if let Some(report) = outcome.report {
            super::core_io::print(&report)?;
        } else if outcome.accepted {
            shell.status(
                "Finished",
                format!("check in {:.2}s", started.elapsed().as_secs_f64()),
            );
        }
    }
    Ok(if outcome.accepted {
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        ExitCode::FAILURE
    })
}

struct CliOutcome {
    accepted: bool,
    beta: bool,
    report: Option<CheckReport>,
}

struct CliConsumer<'a> {
    name: &'a str,
    source: &'a str,
    json: bool,
    shell: &'a mut Shell,
}

impl SourceCheckConsumer for CliConsumer<'_> {
    type Output = super::Result<CliOutcome>;

    fn parsed(&mut self, tokens: usize, nodes: usize) {
        if !self.json {
            self.shell
                .verbose_status("Parsed", format!("{tokens} tokens, {nodes} nodes"));
        }
    }

    fn beta(
        self,
        checked: Option<&mori_checker::Checked<'_>>,
        diagnostics: Vec<MoriDiagnostic>,
    ) -> Self::Output {
        let report = self.json.then(|| {
            check_source::beta_report(self.name.to_owned(), self.source, checked, &diagnostics)
        });
        let accepted = finish(self.shell, self.name, self.source, diagnostics, self.json);
        Ok(CliOutcome {
            accepted,
            beta: true,
            report,
        })
    }

    fn core(
        self,
        result: Result<mori_core::Program, mori_core::Error>,
        staged: bool,
    ) -> Self::Output {
        if self.json {
            let report = check_source::core_report(self.name, self.source, &result, staged);
            super::core_io::print(&report)?;
        } else {
            match &result {
                Ok(_) => self.shell.status("Finished", "bounded core check"),
                Err(error) => self.shell.error(error),
            }
        }
        Ok(CliOutcome {
            accepted: result.is_ok(),
            beta: false,
            report: None,
        })
    }
}

/// Renders the diagnostics, unless the report is JSON. True when there are none.
fn finish(
    shell: &mut Shell,
    name: &str,
    source: &str,
    diagnostics: Vec<MoriDiagnostic>,
    json: bool,
) -> bool {
    if diagnostics.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    if !json {
        let count = diagnostics.len();
        for diagnostic in diagnostics {
            shell.report(&diagnostic.with_source_code(NamedSource::new(
                crate::display::text(name),
                source.to_owned(),
            )));
        }
        let plural = if count == 1 { "" } else { "s" };
        shell.error(format!(
            "could not check `{name}` due to {count} previous error{plural}"
        ));
    }
    false
}

//! Shared source-profile dispatch and the existing check report formats.

use mori_diagnostics::MoriDiagnostic;

use crate::json::CheckReport;

/// Consume checked values while the Beta AST they borrow is still alive.
/// Reports remain optional: a human consumer can render diagnostics directly.
pub(super) trait SourceCheckConsumer {
    type Output;

    /// Called after Beta parsing, before its checker starts.
    fn parsed(&mut self, _tokens: usize, _nodes: usize) {}

    fn beta(
        self,
        checked: Option<&mori_checker::Checked<'_>>,
        diagnostics: Vec<MoriDiagnostic>,
    ) -> Self::Output;

    fn core(
        self,
        result: Result<mori_core::Program, mori_core::Error>,
        staged: bool,
    ) -> Self::Output;
}

/// Select exactly the same Beta, Core1 or staged Core2 path as `mori check`.
pub(super) fn dispatch<C: SourceCheckConsumer>(source: &str, mut consumer: C) -> C::Output {
    if mori_lexer::first_token_text(source).is_ok_and(|token| token == "language") {
        let staged = mori_core::language(source).is_ok_and(|language| language == "moriarty/2");
        let result = if staged {
            mori_core::stage::load(source).map(|program| program.program().clone())
        } else {
            mori_core::parse(source)
        };
        return consumer.core(result, staged);
    }
    match mori_parser::parse(source) {
        Err(error) => consumer.beta(None, vec![error]),
        Ok(ast) => {
            consumer.parsed(ast.tokens.len(), ast.nodes.len());
            let mori_checker::CheckResult {
                checked,
                diagnostics,
            } = mori_checker::check(&ast);
            consumer.beta(Some(&checked), diagnostics)
        }
    }
}

/// Preserve the Beta struct's serialization order and diagnostic/span mapping.
pub(super) fn beta_report(
    file: String,
    source: &str,
    checked: Option<&mori_checker::Checked<'_>>,
    diagnostics: &[MoriDiagnostic],
) -> CheckReport {
    CheckReport::new(file, source, checked, diagnostics)
}

/// Construct the existing Core JSON object only when a consumer requests it.
pub(super) fn core_report(
    file: &str,
    source: &str,
    result: &Result<mori_core::Program, mori_core::Error>,
    staged: bool,
) -> serde_json::Value {
    let mut report = match result {
        Ok(program) => {
            serde_json::json!({"status":"accepted", "file":file,"source_hash":mori_core::intent::hash_bytes(source.as_bytes()),"language":program.language,"agreement":program.name,"actions":program.actions,"diagnostics":[]})
        }
        Err(error) => {
            serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","file":file,"diagnostics":[error]})
        }
    };
    if staged {
        let object = report
            .as_object_mut()
            .expect("stage reports are JSON objects");
        for (name, value) in mori_core::stage::STAGE_LABELS {
            object.insert(name.into(), serde_json::Value::String(value.into()));
        }
    }
    report
}

#[cfg(feature = "native")]
use super::core_io;
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
use crate::error::CliError;
use crate::shell::Shell;
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
use std::path::Path;
use std::{path::PathBuf, process::ExitCode};

#[derive(Debug, clap::Args)]
pub struct Args {
    pub file: PathBuf,
    /// Exact target profile JSON with network, anchor and compiler limits
    #[arg(long)]
    pub target: PathBuf,
    /// New output directory; refuses to overwrite existing artifacts
    #[arg(long)]
    pub out: PathBuf,
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn run(args: Args, shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    let source = core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
    if mori_core::language(&source).is_ok_and(|language| language == "moriarty/2") {
        let target: mori_backend::Target = core_io::read_json(&args.target)?;
        let artifact = mori_backend::stage::compile_staged(&source, &target, &args.out)
            .map_err(core_io::operation)?;
        let manifest = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&artifact).map_err(core_io::operation)?;
        std::fs::create_dir(&args.out).map_err(|source| CliError::Write {
            path: args.out.clone(),
            source,
        })?;
        publish_staged_artifact(&artifact, &manifest, &args.out)?;
        shell.status(
            "Compiled",
            format!(
                "{} circuits into {}",
                artifact.circuits.len(),
                args.out.display()
            ),
        );
        return Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS);
    }
    let program = mori_core::parse(&source).map_err(core_io::operation)?;
    let target: mori_backend::Target = core_io::read_json(&args.target)?;
    // The trusted Target selects the mode explicitly; a signed Target never
    // reaches the unsigned compiler.
    let reported = mori_backend::source_projection::compile_reported(&program, &target)
        .map_err(core_io::operation)?;
    let artifact = reported.artifact;
    let projection = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&serde_json::json!({
        "source_hash": mori_core::intent::hash_bytes(source.as_bytes()),
        "compilation": reported.source_projection,
    }))
    .map_err(core_io::operation)?;
    // Compile and serialize fully before touching the destination.
    let manifest = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&artifact).map_err(core_io::operation)?;
    std::fs::create_dir(&args.out).map_err(|source| CliError::Write {
        path: args.out.clone(),
        source,
    })?;
    publish_artifact(&artifact, &manifest, Some(&projection), &args.out)?;
    shell.status(
        "Compiled",
        format!(
            "{} circuits into {}",
            artifact.circuits.len(),
            args.out.display()
        ),
    );
    Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
}

// The caller has reserved a new directory after all input/compiler preflight.
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
fn publish_artifact(
    artifact: &mori_backend::Artifact,
    manifest: &str,
    projection: Option<&str>,
    out: &Path,
) -> super::Result<()> {
    for (index, circuit) in artifact.circuits.iter().enumerate() {
        let path = out.join(format!("{index:03}-{}.zkir", circuit.action));
        super::proof_io::publish_new(&path, circuit.zkir.as_bytes())?;
    }
    if let Some(projection) = projection {
        let path = out.join("source-projection.json");
        super::proof_io::publish_new(&path, projection.as_bytes())?;
    }
    let path = out.join("artifact.json");
    // The manifest is the completion marker; publish it after every circuit.
    super::proof_io::publish_new(&path, manifest.as_bytes())?;
    Ok(())
}

// The staged compiler returns the real artifact; publication stays in the CLI.
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
fn publish_staged_artifact(
    artifact: &mori_backend::stage::StagedArtifact,
    manifest: &str,
    out: &Path,
) -> super::Result<()> {
    for (index, circuit) in artifact.circuits.iter().enumerate() {
        let path = out.join(format!(
            "{index:03}-{}.s{}.zkir",
            circuit.action, circuit.segment
        ));
        super::proof_io::publish_new(&path, circuit.zkir.as_bytes())?;
    }
    // As in publish_artifact, the manifest is the completion marker.
    super::proof_io::publish_new(&out.join("artifact.json"), manifest.as_bytes())?;
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "native"))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    struct Reserved(PathBuf);
    impl Reserved {
        fn new() -> Self {
            let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
                "mori-compile-leaves-{}-{}",
                std::process::id(),
                NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
            ));
            std::fs::create_dir(&p).unwrap();
            Self(p)
        }
    }
    impl Drop for Reserved {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }
    fn artifact() -> (mori_backend::Artifact, String) {
        let manifest = include_str!(concat!(
            env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
            "/../fixtures/publication/transport-artifact.json"
        ));
        let artifact = serde_json::from_str::<mori_backend::Artifact>(manifest).unwrap();
        (artifact, manifest.to_owned())
    }
    #[test]
    fn raced_files_at_first_second_and_manifest_are_never_clobbered() {
        let (a, m) = artifact();
        for leaf in ["000-z_first.zkir", "001-a_second.zkir", "artifact.json"] {
            let d = Reserved::new();
            let p = d.0.join(leaf);
            std::fs::write(&p, b"third-party sentinel").unwrap();
            std::fs::write(d.0.join("unrelated"), b"user addition").unwrap();
            assert!(
                publish_artifact(&a, &m, None, &d.0).is_err(),
                "raced {leaf} must refuse"
            );
            assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&p).unwrap(), b"third-party sentinel");
            assert_eq!(
                std::fs::read(d.0.join("unrelated")).unwrap(),
                b"user addition"
            );
            if leaf != "artifact.json" {
                assert!(!d.0.join("artifact.json").exists());
            }
            let completed = match leaf {
                "000-z_first.zkir" => 0,
                "001-a_second.zkir" => 1,
                _ => 2,
            };
            assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&d.0).unwrap().count(), completed + 2);
            for (i, c) in a.circuits.iter().take(completed).enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(
                    std::fs::read(d.0.join(format!("{i:03}-{}.zkir", c.action))).unwrap(),
                    c.zkir.as_bytes()
                );
            }
        }
    }
    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn raced_symlinks_dangling_symlinks_and_directories_are_preserved() {
        let (a, m) = artifact();
        for leaf in ["001-a_second.zkir", "artifact.json"] {
            for kind in ["symlink", "dangling", "directory", "directory-symlink"] {
                let d = Reserved::new();
                let external = Reserved::new();
                let target = external.0.join("target");
                let p = d.0.join(leaf);
                match kind {
                    "symlink" => {
                        std::fs::write(&target, b"external sentinel").unwrap();
                        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&target, &p).unwrap();
                    }
                    "dangling" => std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&target, &p).unwrap(),
                    "directory" => std::fs::create_dir(&p).unwrap(),
                    _ => {
                        std::fs::create_dir(&target).unwrap();
                        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&target, &p).unwrap();
                    }
                }
                assert!(publish_artifact(&a, &m, None, &d.0).is_err());
                if kind == "directory" {
                    assert!(p.is_dir());
                    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&p).unwrap().count(), 0);
                } else {
                    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_link(&p).unwrap(), target);
                }
                if kind == "symlink" {
                    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&target).unwrap(), b"external sentinel");
                } else if kind == "dangling" {
                    assert!(!target.exists());
                }
                if leaf != "artifact.json" {
                    assert!(!d.0.join("artifact.json").exists());
                }
                assert_eq!(
                    std::fs::read(d.0.join("000-z_first.zkir")).unwrap(),
                    a.circuits[0].zkir.as_bytes()
                );
                assert_eq!(
                    std::fs::read_dir(&d.0).unwrap().count(),
                    if leaf == "artifact.json" { 3 } else { 2 }
                );
            }
        }
    }
    #[test]
    fn final_manifest_follows_all_complete_ordered_circuits() {
        let (a, m) = artifact();
        let d = Reserved::new();
        publish_artifact(&a, &m, None, &d.0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(d.0.join("artifact.json")).unwrap(),
            m.as_bytes()
        );
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&d.0).unwrap().count(), 3);
        for (i, c) in a.circuits.iter().enumerate() {
            assert_eq!(
                std::fs::read(d.0.join(format!("{i:03}-{}.zkir", c.action))).unwrap(),
                c.zkir.as_bytes()
            );
        }
    }
    #[test]
    fn source_projection_is_published_with_complete_circuits_and_manifest() {
        let (a, m) = artifact();
        let d = Reserved::new();
        let projection = "{\"transport_fixture\":\"projection\"}\n";
        publish_artifact(&a, &m, Some(projection), &d.0).unwrap();
        for (leaf, bytes) in [
            (
                "000-z_first.zkir",
                "publication fixture: z_first\nopaque UTF-8: α\n",
            ),
            (
                "001-a_second.zkir",
                "publication fixture: a_second\nopaque UTF-8: β\n",
            ),
            ("source-projection.json", projection),
            ("artifact.json", m.as_str()),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(std::fs::read(d.0.join(leaf)).unwrap(), bytes.as_bytes());
        }
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&d.0).unwrap().count(), 4);
    }
}

use crate::error::CliError;
use serde::{Serialize, de::DeserializeOwned};
use std::path::Path;

pub fn read_source(path: &Path) -> super::Result<String> {
    use std::io::Read;
    let file = std::fs::File::open(path).map_err(|source| CliError::Read {
        path: path.into(),
        source,
    })?;
    let mut source = String::new();
    file.take(1_048_577)
        .read_to_string(&mut source)
        .map_err(|source| CliError::Read {
            path: path.into(),
            source,
        })?;
    if source.len() > 1_048_576 {
        return Err(operation("input file exceeds 1 MiB"));
    }
    Ok(source)
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "native"))]
mod key_export_diagnostic_tests {
    use super::*;
    use mori_ledger::{Error, KeyExportDiagnostic, KeyExportFailureReason, KeyExportKind};

    fn refusal(action: &str, key_kind: KeyExportKind, reason: KeyExportFailureReason) -> Error {
        let cap_refusal = reason == KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded;
        Error::new("native-proving", "generated-key-size-or-encode").with_key_export(
            KeyExportDiagnostic {
                action: action.into(),
                key_kind,
                discovered_degree: 0,
                byte_cap: 3,
                accepted_bytes: 2,
                failed_write_bytes: (reason != KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization).then_some(2),
                attempted_minimum: cap_refusal.then_some(4),
                reason,
            },
        )
    }
    #[test]
    fn key_export_cli_preserves_category_and_discriminates_reasons() {
        for kind in [KeyExportKind::Prover, KeyExportKind::Verifier] {
            for (reason, label) in [
                (KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded, "byte-cap-exceeded"),
                (
                    KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCountOverflow,
                    "byte-count-overflow",
                ),
                (
                    KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization,
                    "serialization-failure",
                ),
            ] {
                let report = ledger_operation(refusal("settle", kind, reason)).to_string();
                let kind = if kind == KeyExportKind::Prover {
                    "prover"
                } else {
                    "verifier"
                };
                assert!(report.starts_with("mori::command: mori::ledger::native-proving: generated-key-size-or-encode; "), "{report}");
                assert!(report.contains(&format!("action=\"settle\" key-kind={kind} discovered-degree=0 byte-cap=3 accepted-bytes=2 reason={label}")), "{report}");
                assert_eq!(
                    report.contains("failed-write-bytes=2"),
                    reason != KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization
                );
                assert_eq!(
                    report.contains("attempted-minimum=4"),
                    reason == KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded
                );
            }
        }
        let legacy = Error::new("native-proving", "sdk-keygen");
        assert_eq!(
            ledger_operation(legacy.clone()).to_string(),
            operation(legacy).to_string()
        );
    }
    #[test]
    fn key_export_cli_action_is_ascii_json_escaped_once_and_round_trips() {
        let action = "settle\"\\\nforged\r\u{1b}[31m\u{7f}\u{85}\u{202e}\u{1f9ea}";
        let error = refusal(
            action,
            KeyExportKind::Verifier,
            KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded,
        );
        assert_eq!(error.key_export().unwrap().action, action);
        let report = ledger_operation(error).to_string();
        let encoded = report
            .split_once("; action=")
            .unwrap()
            .1
            .split_once(" key-kind=")
            .unwrap()
            .0;
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<String>(encoded).unwrap(), action);
        assert!(report.is_ascii(), "{report}");
        assert!(report.chars().all(|c| !c.is_control()), "{report}");
        assert!(encoded.contains(r"\u0085"));
        assert!(encoded.contains(r"\u202e"));
        assert!(encoded.contains(r"\ud83e\uddea"));
        assert_eq!(
            encoded,
            r#""settle\"\\\nforged\r\u001b[31m\u007f\u0085\u202e\ud83e\uddea""#
        );
    }
    #[test]
    fn key_export_quiet_shell_reports_safe_metadata_on_actual_stderr() {
        const CHILD: &str = "MORI_KEY_EXPORT_DIAGNOSTIC_REPORT_CHILD";
        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_some() {
            let report = ledger_operation(refusal(
                "settle\n\u{1b}\u{202e}",
                KeyExportKind::Prover,
                KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded,
            ));
            let mut shell = crate::shell::Shell::new(
                crate::shell::Verbosity::Quiet,
                anstream::ColorChoice::Never,
            );
            shell.report(&report);
            return;
        }
        let output = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
            .args(["--exact", "commands::core_io::key_export_diagnostic_tests::key_export_quiet_shell_reports_safe_metadata_on_actual_stderr", "--nocapture"])
            .env(CHILD, "1").output().unwrap();
        assert!(output.status.success());
        let stderr = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).unwrap();
        // The trusted renderer adds Unicode box drawing and may wrap a field
        // across lines. Inspect its joined content, plus raw hostile controls.
        let content: String = stderr
            .lines()
            .map(|line| {
                line.strip_prefix("  │ ")
                    .or_else(|| line.strip_prefix("  × "))
                    .unwrap_or(line)
            })
            .collect();
        for value in [
            "generated-key-size-or-encode",
            "key-kind=prover",
            "discovered-degree=0",
            "byte-cap=3",
            "accepted-bytes=2",
            "byte-cap-exceeded",
            "failed-write-bytes=2",
            "attempted-minimum=4",
            r#"action="settle\n\u001b\u202e""#,
        ] {
            assert!(content.contains(value), "{stderr}");
        }
        assert!(!stderr.contains(['\u{1b}', '\u{85}', '\u{202e}']));
        assert!(!stderr.contains("key-bytes"));
    }
}
pub fn operation(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> mori_diagnostics::Report {
    CliError::Operation {
        code: "mori::command".into(),
        message: crate::display::text(&error.to_string()),
    }
    .into()
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn ledger_operation(error: mori_ledger::Error) -> mori_diagnostics::Report {
    use mori_ledger::{DegreeRefusalReason, KeyExportFailureReason, KeyExportKind};
    let mut message = crate::display::text(&error.to_string());
    if let Some(diagnostic) = error.degree_refusal() {
        let reason = match diagnostic.reason {
            DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded => "caller-ceiling-exceeded",
            DegreeRefusalReason::UnsupportedPinnedDegree => "unsupported-pinned-degree",
            DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { .. } => "cached-degree-mismatch",
        };
        // Quote the exact source identity once; operation() would escape this
        // already-rendered identity again. All remaining context is metadata.
        message.push_str(&format!(
            "; action={} discovered-degree={} caller-ceiling={} pinned-supported={} reason={reason}",
            review_identity(&diagnostic.action),
            diagnostic.discovered_degree,
            diagnostic.caller_ceiling,
            diagnostic.pinned_supported,
        ));
        if let DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { cached_degree } = diagnostic.reason {
            message.push_str(&format!(" cached-degree={cached_degree}"));
        }
    }
    if let Some(diagnostic) = error.key_export() {
        let kind = match diagnostic.key_kind {
            KeyExportKind::Prover => "prover",
            KeyExportKind::Verifier => "verifier",
        };
        let reason = match diagnostic.reason {
            KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded => "byte-cap-exceeded",
            KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCountOverflow => "byte-count-overflow",
            KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization => "serialization-failure",
        };
        message.push_str(&format!(
            "; action={} key-kind={kind} discovered-degree={} byte-cap={} accepted-bytes={} reason={reason}",
            key_export_identity(&diagnostic.action),
            diagnostic.discovered_degree,
            diagnostic.byte_cap,
            diagnostic.accepted_bytes,
        ));
        if let Some(bytes) = diagnostic.failed_write_bytes {
            message.push_str(&format!(" failed-write-bytes={bytes}"));
        }
        if let Some(minimum) = diagnostic.attempted_minimum {
            message.push_str(&format!(" attempted-minimum={minimum}"));
        }
    }
    CliError::Operation {
        code: "mori::command".into(),
        message,
    }
    .into()
}
/// JSON escaping quotes/controls once, with UTF-16 escapes for non-ASCII
/// identities. This remains valid JSON even for supplementary Unicode scalars.
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
fn key_export_identity(value: &str) -> String {
    let json = serde_json::to_string(value).expect("serializing a string cannot fail");
    let mut escaped = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    for character in json.chars() {
        if character.is_ascii() && !character.is_control() {
            escaped.push(character);
        } else {
            let mut units = [0; 2];
            for unit in character.encode_utf16(&mut units) {
                use std::fmt::Write;
                write!(escaped, "\\u{unit:04x}").expect("writing to a String cannot fail");
            }
        }
    }
    escaped
}
pub fn read_json<T: DeserializeOwned>(path: &Path) -> super::Result<T> {
    let source = read_source(path)?;
    let value = mori_core::json::parse(&source).map_err(operation)?;
    serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(operation)
}
pub fn program(path: &Path) -> super::Result<(String, mori_core::Program)> {
    let source = read_source(path)?;
    let program = mori_core::parse(&source).map_err(operation)?;
    Ok((source, program))
}
pub fn print<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> super::Result<()> {
    let display = mori_core::json::export(value).map_err(operation)?;
    println!("{display}");
    Ok(())
}
/// Trusted signed Target, separately supplied expected authority and logical time.
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn signed_target(path: &Path) -> super::Result<mori_backend::Target> {
    let target: mori_backend::Target = read_json(path)?;
    if target.signed_policy.is_none() {
        return Err(operation(
            "the signed profile requires a trusted Target with signed_policy",
        ));
    }
    Ok(target)
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn authority(path: &Path) -> super::Result<mori_backend::authorization::ExpectedAuthority> {
    mori_backend::authorization::ExpectedAuthority::from_json(&read_source(path)?)
        .map_err(operation)
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn signed_intent(path: &Path) -> super::Result<mori_backend::authorization::SignedIntent> {
    mori_backend::authorization::SignedIntent::from_json(&read_source(path)?).map_err(operation)
}
/// Quote display identities without giving source text terminal control.
pub fn review_identity(value: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "\"{}\"",
        value
            .chars()
            .flat_map(char::escape_default)
            .collect::<String>()
    )
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "native"))]
mod degree_diagnostic_tests {
    use super::*;
    use mori_ledger::{DegreeRefusalDiagnostic, DegreeRefusalReason, Error};

    fn refusal(action: &str, reason: DegreeRefusalReason) -> Error {
        let (discovered_degree, caller_ceiling, pinned_supported) = match reason {
            DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded => (14, 13, true),
            DegreeRefusalReason::UnsupportedPinnedDegree => (20, 25, false),
            DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { .. } => (13, 13, true),
        };
        Error::new("local-deployment", "exact-degree-unavailable").with_degree_refusal(
            DegreeRefusalDiagnostic {
                action: action.into(),
                discovered_degree,
                caller_ceiling,
                pinned_supported,
                reason,
            },
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn ledger_conversion_preserves_category_and_complete_permitted_context() {
        for (reason, context) in [
            (
                DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded,
                "discovered-degree=14 caller-ceiling=13 pinned-supported=true reason=caller-ceiling-exceeded",
            ),
            (
                DegreeRefusalReason::UnsupportedPinnedDegree,
                "discovered-degree=20 caller-ceiling=25 pinned-supported=false reason=unsupported-pinned-degree",
            ),
            (
                DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { cached_degree: 12 },
                "discovered-degree=13 caller-ceiling=13 pinned-supported=true reason=cached-degree-mismatch cached-degree=12",
            ),
        ] {
            let report = ledger_operation(refusal("freeze", reason));
            assert_eq!(
                report.to_string(),
                format!(
                    "mori::command: mori::ledger::local-deployment: exact-degree-unavailable; action=\"freeze\" {context}"
                )
            );
        }
        let legacy = Error::new("local-deployment", "selected-action");
        assert_eq!(
            ledger_operation(legacy.clone()).to_string(),
            operation(legacy).to_string()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn hostile_action_is_exact_in_api_and_escaped_once_in_command_report() {
        let action = "freeze\u{1b}[31m\nforged\r\"\\\u{85}\u{202e}";
        let error = refusal(action, DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded);
        assert_eq!(error.degree_refusal().unwrap().action, action);
        let message = ledger_operation(error).to_string();
        assert!(
            message.contains(r#"action="freeze\u{1b}[31m\nforged\r\"\\\u{85}\u{202e}""#),
            "{message}"
        );
        assert!(message.chars().all(|c| !c.is_control()));
        assert_eq!(
            message,
            r#"mori::command: mori::ledger::local-deployment: exact-degree-unavailable; action="freeze\u{1b}[31m\nforged\r\"\\\u{85}\u{202e}" discovered-degree=14 caller-ceiling=13 pinned-supported=true reason=caller-ceiling-exceeded"#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn quiet_shell_reports_constructed_degree_refusal_on_stderr() {
        const CHILD: &str = "MORI_DEGREE_DIAGNOSTIC_REPORT_CHILD";
        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_some() {
            let report = ledger_operation(refusal(
                "freeze",
                DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded,
            ));
            let mut shell = crate::shell::Shell::new(
                crate::shell::Verbosity::Quiet,
                anstream::ColorChoice::Never,
            );
            shell.report(&report);
            return;
        }
        let output = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
            .args(["--exact", "commands::core_io::degree_diagnostic_tests::quiet_shell_reports_constructed_degree_refusal_on_stderr", "--nocapture"])
            .env(CHILD, "1").output().unwrap();
        assert!(output.status.success());
        let stderr = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).unwrap();
        for value in [
            "exact-degree-unavailable",
            "action=\"freeze\"",
            "discovered-degree=14",
            "caller-ceiling=13",
            "caller-ceiling-exceeded",
        ] {
            assert!(stderr.contains(value), "{stderr}");
        }
        assert!(!stderr.contains('\u{1b}'));
    }

//! Explicit local transfer presentation consumer of mori-source6.
use std::{io::Write, process::ExitCode};

use mori_core::UInt;
use mori_diagnostics::NamedSource;
use mori_source6::{Allowance, Balance, LocalTransferScenario, Replay, select_transfer};
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::{cli::ActionInput, commands::core_io, shell::Shell};

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct TransferScenario {
    #[serde(rename = "profile")]
    _profile: String,
    #[serde(rename = "kind")]
    _kind: String,
    domain: String,
    asset: String,
    head: String,
    predecessor: String,
    round: UInt,
    balances: [BalanceCell; 3],
    allowance: AllowanceCell,
    replay: ReplayClaim,
    work_remaining: UInt,
    work_spent: UInt,
    post_head: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct BalanceCell {
    account: String,
    amount: UInt,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct AllowanceCell {
    owner: String,
    remaining: UInt,
    spent: UInt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
enum ReplayClaim {
    Unused,
    Consumed,
}

impl TransferScenario {
    fn local(&self) -> LocalTransferScenario<'_> {
        LocalTransferScenario {
            domain: &self.domain,
            asset: &self.asset,
            head: &self.head,
            predecessor: &self.predecessor,
            round: self.round.0,
            balances: self.balances.each_ref().map(|cell| Balance {
                account: &cell.account,
                amount: cell.amount.0,
            }),
            allowance: Allowance {
                owner: &self.allowance.owner,
                remaining: self.allowance.remaining.0,
                spent: self.allowance.spent.0,
            },
            replay: match self.replay {
                ReplayClaim::Unused => Replay::Unused,
                ReplayClaim::Consumed => Replay::Consumed,
            },
            work_remaining: self.work_remaining.0,
            work_spent: self.work_spent.0,
            post_head: &self.post_head,
        }
    }
}

fn scenario_error(code: &str, message: impl Into<String>) -> mori_diagnostics::Report {
    crate::error::CliError::Operation {
        code: format!("mori::command::{code}"),
        message: crate::display::text(&message.into()),
    }
    .into()
}

fn read_scenario(path: &std::path::Path) -> crate::commands::Result<TransferScenario> {
    let raw: serde_json::Value = core_io::read_json(path)?;
    let object = raw.as_object().ok_or_else(|| {
        scenario_error(
            "source6-scenario-profile",
            "Expected a local transfer scenario object.",
        )
    })?;
    if object.get("profile").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        != Some("moriarty-local-scenario/1")
        || object.get("kind").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some("local-stipulation")
    {
        return Err(scenario_error(
            "source6-scenario-profile",
            "Source/6 transfer expansion requires moriarty-local-scenario/1 local-stipulation input.",
        ));
    }
    for field in ["obligation", "candidate_effects"] {
        if object.contains_key(field) {
            return Err(scenario_error(
                "source6-scenario-unsupported",
                format!("The --emit-source6-transfer subset does not support `{field}`."),
            ));
        }
    }
    if object
        .get("balances")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array)
        .is_some_and(|balances| balances.len() != 3)
    {
        return Err(scenario_error(
            "source6-scenario-cells",
            "The transfer subset requires exactly three balance cells: owner, recipient, fee recipient.",
        ));
    }
    serde_json::from_value(raw).map_err(|error| {
        scenario_error(
            "source6-scenario-shape",
            format!("Local transfer scenario shape: {error}"),
        )
    })
}

pub(super) fn run(input: ActionInput, shell: &mut Shell) -> crate::commands::Result<ExitCode> {
    let source = core_io::read_source(&input.file)?;
    let name = crate::display::text(&input.file.display().to_string());
    let selected = match select_transfer(&source, &input.action) {
        Ok(selected) => selected,
        Err(diagnostics) => {
            for diagnostic in diagnostics {
                shell.report(&diagnostic.with_source_code(NamedSource::new(&name, source.clone())));
            }
            return Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE);
        }
    };
    let scenario = read_scenario(&input.scenario)?;
    let expansion = match selected.expand(&scenario.local()) {
        Ok(expansion) => expansion,
        Err(diagnostic) => {
            shell.report(&diagnostic.with_source_code(NamedSource::new(name, source)));
            return Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE);
        }
    };
    // The library includes its final newline. This writes its actual proposal.
    std::io::stdout()
        .lock()
        .write_all(expansion.source6.as_bytes())
        .map_err(core_io::operation)?;
    shell.status(
        "Expanded",
        format!("Source/6 transfer proposal ({})", expansion.qualification),
    );
    Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
}
