//! One module per subcommand. Each defines its `Args` and a `run` function.

use std::process::ExitCode;

use mori_diagnostics::Report;

use crate::cli::Command;
use crate::shell::Shell;

mod call_io;
pub mod capabilities;
pub mod check;
mod check_source;
pub mod compile;
pub mod compile_call;
mod core_io;
pub mod expand;
pub mod format;
pub mod init;
pub mod inspect;
pub mod intent;
pub mod keygen_call;
pub mod keygen_signed_call;
pub mod lsp;
pub mod mcp;
pub mod prepare_call;
pub mod prepare_signed_call;
mod proof_io;
pub mod prove;
pub mod prove_call;
pub mod prove_signed_call;
pub mod replay;
mod signed_call_io;
pub mod simulate;
pub mod test;
pub mod verify;
pub mod verify_call;
pub mod verify_intent;
pub mod verify_signed_call;

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Report>;

pub fn run(command: Command, shell: &mut Shell) -> Result<ExitCode> {
    match command {
        Command::Capabilities(args) => capabilities::run(args, shell),
        Command::Init(args) => init::run(args, shell),
        Command::Check(args) => check::run(args, shell),
        Command::Compile(args) => compile::run(args, shell),
        Command::KeygenSignedCall(args) => keygen_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::PrepareSignedCall(args) => prepare_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::ProveSignedCall(args) => prove_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::VerifySignedCall(args) => verify_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::KeygenCall(args) => keygen_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::ProveCall(args) => prove_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::VerifyCall(args) => verify_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::CompileCall(args) => compile_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::PrepareCall(args) => prepare_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::Prove(args) => prove::run(args, shell),
        Command::Verify(args) => verify::run(args, shell),
        Command::Format(args) => format::run(args, shell),
        Command::Inspect(args) => inspect::run(args, shell),
        Command::Expand(args) => expand::run(args, shell),
        Command::Simulate(args) => simulate::run(args, shell),
        Command::Replay(args) => replay::run(args, shell),
        Command::Test(args) => test::run(args, shell),
        Command::Intent(args) => intent::run(args, shell),
        Command::VerifyIntent(args) => verify_intent::run(args, shell),
        Command::Lsp(args) => lsp::run(args, shell),
        Command::Mcp(args) => mcp::run(args, shell),
    }
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]
fn native_unavailable<T>() -> Result<T> {
    Err(crate::error::CliError::Operation {
        code: "mori::command::native-unavailable".into(),
        message: "This mori build has no Midnight support. Rebuild with the native feature enabled."
            .into(),
    }
    .into())
}

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::ExitCode;

use crate::shell::Shell;

#[derive(Debug, clap::Args)]
pub struct Args {
    /// Source file
    pub file: PathBuf,

    /// Action to run
    #[arg(long, value_name = "NAME", required_unless_present = "resume")]
    pub action: Option<String>,

    /// Scenario JSON with the local state and inputs
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE", required_unless_present = "resume")]
    pub scenario: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Resume a moriarty/2 continuation (local, unauthenticated, consumption untracked)
    #[arg(
        long,
        value_name = "FILE",
        requires = "event",
        conflicts_with_all = ["scenario", "trace", "target", "profile", "authority", "at", "signature"]
    )]
    pub resume: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Stage event JSON for --resume (at most 64 KiB)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE", requires = "resume")]
    pub event: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Generate a complete public replay sidecar against a trusted Target
    #[arg(long)]
    pub trace: bool,
    /// Cap local statement and uncached expression attempts (other costs unmeasured)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "CANONICAL_U128", value_parser = logical_cap, conflicts_with = "trace")]
    pub logical_cap: Option<mori_core::UInt>,
    /// Trusted Target JSON (required with --trace)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub target: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub authorization: super::replay::AuthorizationArgs,
}

impl Args {
    /// Legacy start inputs. Clap requires both whenever --resume is absent.
    fn legacy(&self) -> super::Result<(&str, &Path)> {
        match (self.action.as_deref(), self.scenario.as_deref()) {
            (Some(action), Some(scenario)) => Ok((action, scenario)),
            _ => Err(super::core_io::operation(
                "--action and --scenario are required without --resume",
            )),
        }
    }
}

fn logical_cap(value: &str) -> Result<mori_core::UInt, String> {
    serde_json::from_value(serde_json::Value::String(value.into()))
        .map_err(|_| "expected canonical unsigned decimal string in u128 range".into())
}

pub fn run(args: Args, _shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    // Clap has already refused every --resume/--event conflict, so a
    // malformed invocation reads no file.
    if let Some(resume) = &args.resume {
        return run_resume(&args, resume);
    }
    let (action, scenario_path) = args.legacy()?;
    if args.trace {
        let path = args
            .target
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| super::core_io::operation("--trace requires --target"))?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let target = super::core_io::read_json(path)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let authorization = args.authorization.load(&target)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let scenario = super::core_io::read_json(scenario_path)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        return match mori_backend::replay::generate(
            &source,
            action,
            &scenario,
            &target,
            authorization.as_input(),
        ) {
            Ok(record) => {
                super::core_io::print(&record)?;
                Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
            }
            Err(error) => {
                super::core_io::print(
                    &serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":error}),
                )?;
                Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE)
            }
        };
        #[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]
        {
            let _ = path;
            return super::native_unavailable();
        }
    }
    if args.target.is_some() || args.authorization.present() {
        return Err(super::core_io::operation(
            "--target and signed replay arguments require --trace",
        ));
    }
    let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
    // Hook: /2 routing. A /2 start keeps every core failure labelled.
    if mori_core::language(&source) == Ok(mori_core::stage::LANGUAGE_2) {
        return run_stage_start(&args, &source, action, scenario_path);
    }
    let program = mori_core::parse(&source).map_err(super::core_io::operation)?;
    let scenario = super::core_io::read_json(scenario_path)?;
    if let Some(cap) = args.logical_cap {
        return match mori_core::simulate_metered(&program, action, &scenario, cap) {
            Ok(metered) => {
                super::core_io::print(&serde_json::json!({
                    "status": "accepted", "qualification": "local-reference-execution",
                    "execution": metered.execution, "profile": metered.cost.profile,
                    "logical": {"cap": metered.cost.cap, "used": metered.cost.used}
                }))?;
                Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
            }
            Err(refused) => {
                super::core_io::print(&serde_json::json!({
                    "status": "rejected", "error": refused.error,
                    "profile": refused.cost.profile,
                    "logical": {"cap": refused.cost.cap, "used": refused.cost.used}
                }))?;
                Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE)
            }
        };
    }
    match mori_core::simulate(&program, action, &scenario) {
        Ok(execution) => {
            super::core_io::print(
                &serde_json::json!({"status":"accepted", "qualification":"local-reference-execution", "execution":execution}),
            )?;
            Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
        }
        Err(error) => {
            super::core_io::print(&serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected", "error":error}))?;
            Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE)
        }
    }
}

/// Render the same explicit qualification on every staged public object.
pub(super) fn print_stage_report(mut report: serde_json::Value) -> super::Result<()> {
    let object = report
        .as_object_mut()
        .expect("stage reports are JSON objects");
    for (name, value) in mori_core::stage::STAGE_LABELS {
        object.insert(name.into(), serde_json::Value::String(value.into()));
    }
    super::core_io::print(&report)
}

fn print_stage_result(
    result: Result<mori_core::stage::StageOutcome, mori_core::stage::StageRejection>,
) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    let exit = if result.is_ok() {
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        ExitCode::FAILURE
    };
    super::core_io::print(&mori_core::stage::outcome_report(result))?;
    Ok(exit)
}

/// `--resume`: reads the source, then the continuation, then the event.
/// Bounded-read, strict-decode, load and admission failures are labelled stage
/// rejections; a source the filesystem cannot read keeps the legacy error.
/// Nothing is recorded, so the same file can be resumed again (untracked).
fn run_resume(args: &Args, resume: &Path) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    use mori_core::stage::{self, StageOutcome, StageRejection, decode};
    let event_path = args
        .event
        .as_deref()
        .ok_or_else(|| super::core_io::operation("--resume requires --event"))?;
    let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
    let result = (|| -> Result<StageOutcome, StageRejection> {
        let program = stage::load(&source).map_err(no_work)?;
        let continuation = decode::read_bounded(
            resume,
            decode::MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES,
            decode::CONTINUATION_TOO_LARGE,
        )
        .and_then(|text| decode::continuation(&text))
        .map_err(no_work)?;
        let event =
            decode::read_bounded(event_path, decode::MAX_EVENT_BYTES, decode::EVENT_TOO_LARGE)
                .and_then(|text| decode::event(&text))
                .map_err(no_work)?;
        stage::resume(
            &program,
            continuation,
            event,
            args.action.as_deref(),
            args.logical_cap,
        )
    })();
    print_stage_result(result)
}

/// A `/2` start. Load and scenario failures are labelled stage rejections; the
/// scenario keeps the legacy 1 MiB strict reader.
fn run_stage_start(
    args: &Args,
    source: &str,
    action: &str,
    scenario: &Path,
) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    use mori_core::stage::{self, StageOutcome, StageRejection, decode};
    let result = (|| -> Result<StageOutcome, StageRejection> {
        let program = stage::load(source).map_err(no_work)?;
        let text = decode::read_bounded(scenario, 1_048_576, "Scenario JSON exceeds 1 MiB")
            .map_err(no_work)?;
        let value = mori_core::json::parse(&text).map_err(no_work)?;
        let scenario = serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|error| {
            no_work(mori_core::Error {
                code: "mori::core::json".into(),
                message: error.to_string(),
                offset: None,
                step: None,
            })
        })?;
        stage::start(&program, action, scenario, args.logical_cap)
    })();
    print_stage_result(result)
}

/// A refusal before any segment evaluation: no work attempted or committed.
fn no_work(error: mori_core::Error) -> mori_core::stage::StageRejection {
    mori_core::stage::StageRejection {
        error,
        attempted: mori_core::UInt(0),
        committed: mori_core::UInt(0),
    }
}

//! The `--json` report of `mori check`.
//!
//! Spans are UTF-8 byte ranges into the checked file. This format is our own;
//! it is not the TypeScript beta's.

use mori_ast::{Ast, NodeIdx};
use mori_checker::{Checked, DeclIdx, Support};
use mori_diagnostics::{Diagnostic, MoriDiagnostic, Severity};
use mori_lexer::TokenIdx;
use serde::Serialize;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct CheckReport {
    /// `accepted` when there are no diagnostics, otherwise `rejected`.
    pub status: &'static str,
    pub file: String,
    /// SHA-256 of the file's bytes, in lowercase hex.
    pub source_hash: String,
    /// Absent when the file did not parse.
    pub agreement: Option<Named>,
    pub declarations: Vec<DeclarationReport>,
    pub actions: Vec<ActionReport>,
    pub diagnostics: Vec<DiagnosticReport>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Span {
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
}

impl From<mori_span::Span> for Span {
    fn from(span: mori_span::Span) -> Self {
        Self {
            start: span.start,
            end: span.end,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Named {
    pub name: String,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct DeclarationReport {
    /// The declaring keyword, such as `asset` or `intent`.
    pub kind: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub span: Span,
    pub name_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct ActionReport {
    pub name: String,
    pub intent: String,
    /// `local_s0` when it runs locally, `specified_only` when it is only
    /// checked; absent when its intent did not check.
    pub support: Option<&'static str>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub name_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct DiagnosticReport {
    pub code: Option<String>,
    pub severity: &'static str,
    pub message: String,
    pub help: Option<String>,
    pub labels: Vec<LabelReport>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct LabelReport {
    pub span: Span,
    pub text: Option<String>,
    pub primary: bool,
}

impl CheckReport {
    pub fn new(
        file: String,
        source: &str,
        checked: Option<&Checked<'_>>,
        diagnostics: &[MoriDiagnostic],
    ) -> Self {
        let source_hash = Sha256::digest(source.as_bytes())
            .iter()
            .map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}"))
            .collect();
        let mut report = Self {
            status: if diagnostics.is_empty() {
                "accepted"
            } else {
                "rejected"
            },
            file,
            source_hash,
            agreement: None,
            declarations: Vec::new(),
            actions: Vec::new(),
            diagnostics: diagnostics.iter().map(DiagnosticReport::new).collect(),
        };
        if let Some(checked) = checked {
            report.fill(checked);
        }
        report
    }

    fn fill(&mut self, checked: &Checked<'_>) {
        let ast = checked.ast;
        let name_token = ast.main_token(NodeIdx::ROOT);
        self.agreement = Some(Named {
            name: ast.token_text(name_token).to_owned(),
            span: token_span(ast, name_token).into(),
        });
        for index in 0..checked.declarations.len() {
            let decl = DeclIdx::new(index);
            let node = checked.declarations.node()[index];
            let keyword = ast.main_token(node);
            self.declarations.push(DeclarationReport {
                kind: ast.token_text(keyword).to_owned(),
                name: checked.name(decl).to_owned(),
                span: ast.span(node).into(),
                name_span: token_span(ast, ast.token_after(keyword, 1)).into(),
            });
        }
        for (&node, &support) in checked.actions.node().iter().zip(checked.actions.support()) {
            let keyword = ast.main_token(node);
            self.actions.push(ActionReport {
                name: ast.token_text(ast.token_after(keyword, 1)).to_owned(),
                intent: ast.token_text(ast.token_after(keyword, 3)).to_owned(),
                support: support.map(|support| match support {
                    Support::LocalS0 => "local_s0",
                    Support::SpecifiedOnly => "specified_only",
                }),
                span: ast.span(node).into(),
                name_span: token_span(ast, ast.token_after(keyword, 1)).into(),
            });
        }
    }
}

impl DiagnosticReport {
    fn new(diagnostic: &MoriDiagnostic) -> Self {
        let severity = match diagnostic.severity() {
            Some(Severity::Warning) => "warning",
            Some(Severity::Advice) => "advice",
            _ => "error",
        };
        let mut labels: Vec<LabelReport> = diagnostic
            .labels()
            .map(|labels| {
                labels
                    .map(|label| LabelReport {
                        span: Span {
                            start: to_u32(label.offset()),
                            end: to_u32(label.offset() + label.len()),
                        },
                        text: label.label().map(str::to_owned),
                        primary: label.primary(),
                    })
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        // Every diagnostic reports one primary location: the marked label, or
        // else the first.
        if !labels.iter().any(|label| label.primary)
            && let Some(first) = labels.first_mut()
        {
            first.primary = true;
        }
        Self {
            code: diagnostic.code().map(|code| code.to_string()),
            severity,
            message: diagnostic.to_string(),
            help: diagnostic.help().map(|help| help.to_string()),
            labels,
        }
    }
}

fn token_span(ast: &Ast<'_>, token: TokenIdx) -> mori_span::Span {
    ast.tokens.span(token, ast.source)
}

/// Sources are at most 65,536 bytes, so offsets fit in `u32`.
fn to_u32(offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(offset).expect("source offsets fit in u32")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::CheckReport;

    /// Checks the source and snapshots its JSON report, recording the source.
    macro_rules! assert_report_snapshot {
        ($source:literal) => {{
            let source = indoc::indoc!($source);
            let report = match mori_parser::parse(source) {
                Err(error) => CheckReport::new("test.mori".to_owned(), source, None, &[error]),
                Ok(ast) => {
                    let result = mori_checker::check(&ast);
                    CheckReport::new("test.mori".to_owned(), source, Some(&result.checked), &result.diagnostics)
                }
            };
            insta::with_settings!({
                description => format!("Code:\n\n{source}"),
                omit_expression => true,
            }, {
                insta::assert_snapshot!(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report).unwrap());
            });
        }};
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepted_report() {
        assert_report_snapshot!(
            r#"
            profile "moriarty-beta/1";
            agreement Oracle {
              domain Preview = { id: "preview", chain: "midnight", network: "preview" };
              observation price = { id: "price", domain: Preview };
              intent read = { operation: oracle.select(observation: price) };
              action fetch uses read;
            }
            "#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejected_report() {
        assert_report_snapshot!(
            r#"
            profile "moriarty-beta/1";
            agreement Invoice {
              const price = 10;
              const price = pirce;
            }
            "#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unparsable_report() {
        assert_report_snapshot!(
            r#"
            profile "moriarty-beta/1";
            agreement Invoice {
              const price = 10
            "#
        );
    }
}

use std::process::ExitCode;

use clap::Parser;

use crate::cli::Cli;
use crate::shell::Shell;

mod cli;
mod commands;
mod display;
mod error;
mod json;
mod shell;
mod styles;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    let mut shell = Shell::new(cli.global.verbosity(), cli.global.color.into());

    match commands::run(cli.command, &mut shell) {
        Ok(code) => code,
        Err(report) => {
            shell.report(&report);
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

//! Cargo-style status output on stderr.

use std::fmt::Display;
use std::io::{self, Stderr, Write};

use anstream::{AutoStream, ColorChoice};
use anstyle::Style;
use mori_diagnostics::Report;
use mori_diagnostics::render::{self, WIDTH};

use crate::styles;

/// Width of the right-aligned verb column, matching cargo.
const VERB_WIDTH: usize = 12;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Verbosity {
    Quiet,
    Normal,
    Verbose,
}

/// Writes status lines such as `    Checking invoice.mori` to stderr.
///
/// Command results go to stdout and never pass through the shell. Output is
/// best effort: if stderr cannot be written, there is nowhere to report it.
pub struct Shell {
    err: AutoStream<Stderr>,
    verbosity: Verbosity,
}

impl Shell {
    pub fn new(verbosity: Verbosity, color: ColorChoice) -> Self {
        Self {
            err: AutoStream::new(io::stderr(), color),
            verbosity,
        }
    }

    /// Prints a right-aligned green verb followed by a message.
    pub fn status(&mut self, verb: &str, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity != Verbosity::Quiet {
            self.aligned(verb, styles::HEADER, message);
        }
    }

    /// Like [`Shell::status`], but only under `--verbose`.
    pub fn verbose_status(&mut self, verb: &str, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity == Verbosity::Verbose {
            self.aligned(verb, styles::HEADER, message);
        }
    }

    #[expect(dead_code, reason = "used once a command prints notes")]
    pub fn note(&mut self, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity != Verbosity::Quiet {
            self.prefixed("note", styles::HEADER, message);
        }
    }

    #[expect(dead_code, reason = "used once a command emits warnings")]
    pub fn warn(&mut self, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity != Verbosity::Quiet {
            self.prefixed("warning", styles::WARN, message);
        }
    }

    /// Prints an error line. Errors are shown even under `--quiet`.
    pub fn error(&mut self, message: impl Display) {
        self.prefixed("error", styles::ERROR, message);
    }

    /// Renders an error report, wrapped to the terminal width up to 80 columns.
    /// Errors are shown even under `--quiet`.
    pub fn report(&mut self, report: &Report) {
        let width = terminal_size::terminal_size_of(io::stderr())
            .map_or(WIDTH, |(width, _)| usize::from(width.0));
        let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{}", render::render_colored(report, width));
    }

    /// Prints `hunks` as `cargo fmt --check` does, indented to line up with a
    /// diagnostic's message.
    pub fn diff(&mut self, file: &str, hunks: &[mori_fmt::Hunk]) {
        const INDENT: &str = "    ";
        for hunk in hunks {
            let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{INDENT}Diff in {file}:{}:", hunk.line);
            for (change, line) in &hunk.lines {
                let (sign, style) = match change {
                    mori_fmt::Change::Context => (' ', Style::new()),
                    mori_fmt::Change::Removed => ('-', styles::REMOVED),
                    mori_fmt::Change::Added => ('+', styles::ADDED),
                };
                let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{INDENT}{style}{sign}{line}{style:#}");
            }
        }
        let _ = writeln!(self.err);
    }

    fn aligned(&mut self, verb: &str, style: Style, message: impl Display) {
        let message = crate::display::text(&message.to_string());
        let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{style}{verb:>VERB_WIDTH$}{style:#} {message}");
    }

    fn prefixed(&mut self, label: &str, style: Style, message: impl Display) {
        let message = crate::display::text(&message.to_string());
        let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{style}{label}:{style:#} {message}");
    }
}

//! Public capability consumers only; no compiler, target, SDK or native operation.
use serde_json::Value;
use std::{
    collections::BTreeSet,
    ffi::OsString,
    fs,
    path::PathBuf,
    process::{Command, Output, Stdio},
    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
};

static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
struct Files(PathBuf);
impl Files {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "mori-capabilities-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
        ));
        fs::create_dir(&dir).unwrap();
        Self(dir)
    }
    fn run(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Output {
        Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"))
            .current_dir(&self.0)
            .env("PATH", "")
            .stdin(Stdio::null())
            .args(["--color", "never"])
            .args(args)
            .output()
            .unwrap()
    }
    fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<(OsString, Vec<u8>)> {
        let mut files: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(&self.0)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|entry| {
                let entry = entry.unwrap();
                (entry.file_name(), fs::read(entry.path()).unwrap())
            })
            .collect();
        files.sort();
        files
    }
}
impl Drop for Files {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}
fn json(output: &Output) -> Value {
    assert!(
        output.status.success(),
        "exit {:?}: {}",
        output.status.code(),
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
    );
    assert!(output.stderr.is_empty());
    serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).unwrap()
}
fn row<'a>(report: &'a Value, section: &str, id: &str) -> &'a Value {
    report[section]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .find(|row| row["id"] == id)
        .unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn public_query_distinguishes_profiles_build_consumers_and_unchecked_targets() {
    let f = Files::new();
    fs::write(f.0.join("user-note.txt"), "user content\n").unwrap();
    let before = f.snapshot();
    let output = f.run(&["capabilities", "--json"]);
    let report = json(&output);
    assert_eq!(before, f.snapshot());
    assert!(output.stdout.ends_with(b"\n"));
    assert!(output.stdout.len() < 65_536);
    for args in [
        vec!["capabilities"],
        vec!["--quiet", "capabilities", "--json"],
    ] {
        let next = f.run(&args);
        assert_eq!(json(&next), report);
        assert_eq!(next.stdout, output.stdout);
        assert_eq!(before, f.snapshot());
    }
    let fields: BTreeSet<_> = report
        .as_object()
        .unwrap()
        .keys()
        .map(String::as_str)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        fields,
        BTreeSet::from([
            "format",
            "producer",
            "catalogue",
            "profiles",
            "consumers",
            "targets",
            "otherExecutables",
            "limitations"
        ])
    );
    assert_eq!(report["format"], "moriarty-cli-capabilities/1");
    assert_eq!(report["producer"]["implementation"], "rust-workspace-cli");
    assert_eq!(
        report["producer"]["packageVersion"],
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
    );
    assert!(report["producer"]["binarySourceRevision"].is_null());
    assert_eq!(report["catalogue"]["runtimeEvidence"], "not-included");
    for (name, enabled) in [
        ("native", cfg!(feature = "native")),
        ("source6-expansion", cfg!(feature = "source6-expansion")),
        (
            "core2-disjoint-draft",
            cfg!(feature = "core2-disjoint-draft"),
        ),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(report["producer"]["buildFeatures"][name], enabled);
    }
    for section in ["profiles", "consumers", "targets", "otherExecutables"] {
        let values = report[section].as_array().unwrap();
        let ids: BTreeSet<_> = values
            .iter()
            .map(|value| value["id"].as_str().unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(ids.len(), values.len());
    }
    assert_eq!(report["profiles"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 3);
    assert_eq!(
        row(&report, "profiles", "rust-beta-frontend")["sourceProfile"],
        "moriarty-beta/1"
    );
    assert!(row(&report, "profiles", "rust-beta-frontend")["semanticsProfile"].is_null());
    let transfer = row(&report, "consumers", "beta-to-source6-transfer");
    assert_eq!(transfer["inputProfile"], "moriarty-beta/1");
    assert_eq!(transfer["outputProfile"], "Source/6");
    assert_eq!(
        transfer["availableInBuild"],
        cfg!(feature = "source6-expansion")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        row(&report, "consumers", "core2-disjoint-draft")["availableInBuild"],
        cfg!(feature = "core2-disjoint-draft")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        row(&report, "consumers", "core2-reference")["availableInBuild"],
        true
    );
    assert!(row(&report, "consumers", "core2-reference")["outputProfile"].is_null());
    for (id, artifact) in [
        ("core1-compile", "moriarty-zkir-artifact/3"),
        ("core2-compile", "moriarty-zkir-artifact/4"),
    ] {

#[test]
fn reported_core_profiles_select_real_source_only_cli_consumers() {
    let f = Files::new();
    let report = json(&f.run(&["capabilities", "--json"]));
    for (id, language, semantics, body) in [
        (
            "rust-core1",
            "moriarty/1",
            "moriarty-core/1",
            "next count = count + 1;",
        ),
        (
            "rust-core2",
            "moriarty/2",
            "moriarty-core/2",
            "await review(ok: Bool) when ok; next count = count + 1;",
        ),
    ] {
        let profile = row(&report, "profiles", id);
        assert_eq!(profile["sourceProfile"], language);
        assert_eq!(profile["semanticsProfile"], semantics);
        let source = format!(
            "{}\nagreement CapabilityProbe {{ state count: UInt = 0; action run() {{ {body} }} }}\n",
            profile["sourceHeader"].as_str().unwrap()
        );
        fs::write(f.0.join("source.mori"), source).unwrap();
        let before = f.snapshot();
        let checked = json(&f.run(&["check", "source.mori", "--json"]));
        assert_eq!(checked["status"], "accepted");
        assert_eq!(checked["language"], language);
        let inspected = json(&f.run(&["inspect", "source.mori"]));
        assert_eq!(inspected["language"], language);
        assert_eq!(inspected["semantics"], semantics);
        assert_eq!(inspected.get("enforcement_report"), Some(&Value::Null));
        if language == "moriarty/2" {
            assert_eq!(inspected["status"], "accepted");
            assert_eq!(inspected["qualification"], "local-reference-stage");
            assert_eq!(inspected["authentication"], "none");
            assert_eq!(inspected["consumption"], "untracked");
            assert!(row(&report, "consumers", "core2-inspect")["outputProfile"].is_null());
            assert!(inspected.get("format").is_none());
            assert_eq!(inspected["stage_plan"]["format"], "moriarty-stage-plan/1");
        } else {
            assert!(inspected.get("status").is_none());
            assert_eq!(inspected["qualification"], "source-only-unqualified");
            assert_eq!(inspected["format"], "moriarty-enforcement-report/1");
        }
        assert_eq!(before, f.snapshot());
    }
}

//! Public reference-stage consumers against literals frozen before implementation.
//! No test in this file reaches native, proof, replay, or ledger execution; the
//! H16/H19 `--trace` and `compile-call` requests are refused at the profile first.
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use std::{
    path::PathBuf,
    process::{Command, Output},
    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
};

static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
const DELIVERY: &str = include_str!("../../../examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori");
const RESERVE: &str = include_str!("../../../examples/core/continuations/reserve.mori");
const LEGACY: &str = include_str!("../../../examples/core/continuations/atomic-compatibility.mori");
fn oracle() -> Value {
    serde_json::from_str(include_str!(
        "../../../examples/core/continuations/normal-oracle.json"
    ))
    .unwrap()
}
struct Files(PathBuf);
impl Files {
    fn new(source: &str) -> Self {
        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "mori-core-continuations-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
        ));
        std::fs::create_dir(&path).unwrap();
        let f = Self(path);
        f.write("source.mori", source.as_bytes());
        f
    }
    fn path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.0.join(name)
    }
    fn write(&self, name: &str, bytes: impl AsRef<[u8]>) {
        std::fs::write(self.path(name), bytes).unwrap();
    }
    fn json(&self, name: &str, value: &Value) {
        self.write(name, serde_json::to_vec(value).unwrap());
    }
    fn command(&self, command: &str) -> Command {
        let mut c = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"));
        c.args(["--color", "never", command])
            .arg(self.path("source.mori"));
        c
    }
    fn start(&self, action: &str, opening: &Value, cap: Option<&str>) -> Output {
        self.json("scenario.json", opening);
        let mut c = self.command("simulate");
        c.args(["--action", action, "--scenario"])
            .arg(self.path("scenario.json"));
        if let Some(cap) = cap {
            c.args(["--logical-cap", cap]);
        }
        c.output().unwrap()
    }
    fn resume(&self, continuation: &Value, event: &Value, action: Option<&str>) -> Output {
        self.json("continuation.json", continuation);
        self.json("event.json", event);
        let mut c = self.command("simulate");
        c.arg("--resume")
            .arg(self.path("continuation.json"))
            .arg("--event")
            .arg(self.path("event.json"));
        if let Some(action) = action {
            c.args(["--action", action]);
        }
        c.output().unwrap()
    }
}
impl Drop for Files {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}
fn report(output: &Output) -> Value {
    serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
        panic!(
            "{e}: stdout={} stderr={}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
        )
    })
}
fn accepted(output: &Output) -> Value {
    assert!(
        output.status.success(),
        "{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
    );
    assert!(
        output.stderr.is_empty(),
        "{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
    );
    let r = report(output);
    for (key, expected) in oracle()["normal_output_labels_from_opus"]
        .as_object()
        .unwrap()
    {
        assert_eq!(&r[key], expected, "{key}");
    }
    r
}
fn segment(actual: &Value, expected: &Value) {
    let execution = &actual["execution"];
    assert_eq!(execution["semantics"], "moriarty-core/2");
    for key in ["pre", "post", "effects"] {
        assert_eq!(execution[key], expected[key], "{key}");
    }
    let steps = execution["steps"].as_array().unwrap();
    let wanted = expected["steps"].as_array().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(steps.len(), wanted.len());
    for (step, want) in steps.iter().zip(wanted) {
        for key in ["index", "value", "snapshot", "effects"] {
            assert_eq!(step[key], want[key], "{key}");
        }
    }
}
fn waiting(r: &Value, expected: &Value) {
    assert_eq!(r["status"], "waiting");
    assert_eq!(r["advanced"], expected["advanced"]);
    assert_eq!(
        r["attempted"],
        expected["attempted"].as_u64().unwrap().to_string()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        r["committed"],
        expected["committed"].as_u64().unwrap().to_string()

    let c = &r["continuation"];
    assert_eq!(c["site"], expected["site"]);
    assert_eq!(c["captures"], expected["captures"]);
    assert_eq!(c["boundary"], expected["segment"]["post"]);
    assert_eq!(c["logical"]["committed"], r["committed"]);
    assert_eq!(r["residual"], expected["residual"]);
    assert_eq!(
        r["segment"]["frame_post"],
        json!({"site":expected["site"],"captures":expected["captures"]})
    );
    segment(&r["segment"], &expected["segment"]);
}
fn complete(r: &Value, expected: &Value) {
    assert_eq!(r["status"], "complete");
    assert_eq!(
        r["attempted"],
        expected["attempted"].as_u64().unwrap().to_string()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        r["committed"],
        expected["committed"].as_u64().unwrap().to_string()
    );
    assert_eq!(r["residual"], expected["residual"]);
    assert_eq!(r["segment"]["frame_post"], json!({"site":0,"captures":[]}));
    segment(&r["segment"], &expected["segment"]);
}

            serde_json::to_vec(&mori_backend::Target::ledger9("local", "continuations")).unwrap(),
        );
        let output = f
            .command("compile")
            .arg("--target")
            .arg(f.path("target.json"))
            .arg("--out")
            .arg(f.path("out"))
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        assert!(
            output.status.success(),
            "{}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
        );
        let bytes = std::fs::read(f.path("out/artifact.json")).unwrap();
        let artifact: mori_backend::stage::StagedArtifact = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(artifact.format, "moriarty-zkir-artifact/4");
        assert_eq!(artifact.circuits.len(), costs.len());
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&artifact).unwrap(), bytes);
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read_dir(f.path("out")).unwrap().count(),
            costs.len() + 1
        );
        for (j, circuit) in artifact.circuits.iter().enumerate() {
            assert_eq!(circuit.action, action);
            assert_eq!(circuit.segment as usize, j);
            assert_eq!(circuit.entry_site as usize, j);
            assert_eq!(
                circuit.exit_site as usize,
                if j + 1 == costs.len() { 0 } else { j + 1 }
            );
            assert_eq!(
                std::fs::read(f.path(&format!("out/{j:03}-{action}.s{j}.zkir"))).unwrap(),
                circuit.zkir.as_bytes()
            );
            assert!(!circuit.zkir.is_empty());
        }
        let manifest: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap();
        let logical = manifest["resources"]["logical"][0]["segments"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap();
        for (j, cost) in costs.iter().enumerate() {
            assert_eq!(logical[j]["segment_logical"], *cost);
        }
    }
}

//! Public normal Core/1 reports against complete independent literal oracles.
use serde_json::Value;
use std::{
    fs,
    path::PathBuf,
    process::Command,
    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
};

macro_rules! fixture {
    ($name:literal) => {
        include_bytes!(concat!(
            env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
            "/../fixtures/core-report-contract/",
            $name
        ))
        .as_slice()
    };
}

static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

struct Project {
    root: PathBuf,
    source: PathBuf,
    scenario: PathBuf,
}

impl Project {
    fn new(source_name: &str, source: &[u8], scenario_name: &str, scenario: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "mori-core-report-contract-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
        ));
        fs::create_dir(&root).unwrap();
        let project = Self {
            source: root.join(source_name),
            scenario: root.join(scenario_name),
            root,
        };
        fs::write(&project.source, source).unwrap();
        fs::write(&project.scenario, scenario).unwrap();
        project
    }

    fn assert_case(&self, name: &str, action: &str, cap: Option<&str>, expected_stdout: &[u8]) {
        let mut command = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"));
        command
            .current_dir(&self.root)
            .args(["--color", "never", "simulate"])
            .arg(&self.source)
            .args(["--action", action, "--scenario"])
            .arg(&self.scenario);
        if let Some(cap) = cap {
            command.arg(format!("--logical-cap={cap}"));
        }
        let output = command.output().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            output.status.code(),
            Some(0),
            "{name}: {}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            output.stderr.as_slice(),
            fixture!("empty.stderr.expected.bin"),
            "{name}: stderr"
        );
        let actual: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).unwrap();
        let expected: Value = serde_json::from_slice(expected_stdout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(actual, expected, "{name}: complete JSON report");
        assert_eq!(output.stdout, expected_stdout, "{name}: exact stdout bytes");
    }
}

impl Drop for Project {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.root);
    }
}

#[test]
fn counter_unmetered_and_positive_caps_match_complete_public_reports() {
    let project = Project::new(
        "counter.mori",
        fixture!("counter.mori"),
        "counter-amount7.scenario.json",
        fixture!("counter-amount7.scenario.json"),
    );
    for (name, cap, expected) in [
        (
            "counter-unmetered",
            None,
            fixture!("counter.unmetered.stdout.json"),
        ),
        (
            "counter-cap16",
            Some("16"),
            fixture!("counter.cap16.stdout.json"),
        ),
        (
            "counter-capmax",
            Some("340282366920938463463374607431768211455"),
            fixture!("counter.capmax.stdout.json"),
        ),
    ] {
        project.assert_case(name, "run", cap, expected);
    }
}

#[test]
fn empty_action_preserves_complete_frame_unmetered_and_at_zero_cap() {
    let project = Project::new(
        "empty-frame.mori",
        fixture!("empty-frame.mori"),
        "empty-frame.scenario.json",
        fixture!("empty-frame.scenario.json"),
    );
    for (name, cap, expected) in [
        (
            "empty-unmetered",
            None,
            fixture!("empty.unmetered.stdout.json"),
        ),
        ("empty-cap0", Some("0"), fixture!("empty.cap0.stdout.json")),

#![cfg(feature = "source6-expansion")]

use serde_json::Value;
use std::{
    fs,
    path::PathBuf,
    process::{Command, Output},
    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
};

macro_rules! fixture {
    ($name:literal) => {
        include_bytes!(concat!(
            env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
            "/tests/fixtures/source6-expansion/",
            $name
        ))
        .as_slice()
    };
}

static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

struct Files(PathBuf);

impl Files {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "mori-source6-expand-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed),
        ));
        fs::create_dir(&root).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.join("invoice.mori"), fixture!("invoice.mori")).unwrap();
        fs::write(
            root.join("scenario.json"),
            fixture!("invoice.scenario.json"),
        )
        .unwrap();
        fs::write(root.join("core.mori"), fixture!("core.mori")).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.join("core.json"), fixture!("core.scenario.json")).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.join("repayment.mori"), fixture!("repayment.mori")).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.join("oracle.mori"), fixture!("oracle.mori")).unwrap();
        Self(root)
    }

    fn invoke(&self, arguments: &[&str]) -> Output {
        Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"))
            .current_dir(&self.0)
            .args(["--color", "never"])
            .args(arguments)
            .output()
            .unwrap()
    }
}

impl Drop for Files {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}

fn source6_arguments() -> [&'static str; 7] {
    [
        "expand",
        "invoice.mori",
        "--action",
        "pay",
        "--scenario",
        "scenario.json",
        "--emit-source6-transfer",
    ]
}

#[test]
fn checked_beta_reaches_real_expansion_library_and_raw_stdout() {
    let files = Files::new();
    let check = files.invoke(&["check", "invoice.mori", "--json"]);
    assert_eq!(check.status.code(), Some(0));
    assert!(check.stderr.is_empty());
    let report: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&check.stdout).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(report["status"], "accepted");
    assert_eq!(report["actions"][0]["name"], "pay");
    assert_eq!(report["actions"][0]["support"], "local_s0");

    let expansion = files.invoke(&source6_arguments());
    assert_eq!(expansion.status.code(), Some(0));
    assert_eq!(expansion.stdout.as_slice(), fixture!("invoice.source6"));
    assert_eq!(expansion.stderr.as_slice(), fixture!("source6.stderr.txt"));
}

#[test]
fn explicit_source6_quiet_output_is_raw_source6_text() {
    let files = Files::new();
    let mut arguments = vec!["--quiet"];
    arguments.extend(source6_arguments());
    let expansion = files.invoke(&arguments);
    assert_eq!(expansion.status.code(), Some(0));
    assert_eq!(expansion.stdout.as_slice(), fixture!("invoice.source6"));
    assert!(expansion.stderr.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn core_default_retains_complete_program_bytes() {
    let files = Files::new();
    let output = files.invoke(&[
        "expand",
        "core.mori",
        "--action",
        "noop",
        "--scenario",
        "core.json",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(0));
    assert_eq!(output.stdout.as_slice(), fixture!("core.stdout.json"));
    assert!(output.stderr.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn beta_default_retains_core_parser_refusal_boundary() {
    let files = Files::new();
    let output = files.invoke(&[
        "expand",
        "invoice.mori",
        "--action",
        "pay",
        "--scenario",
        "scenario.json",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(1));
    assert!(output.stdout.is_empty());
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).contains("mori::core::syntax"));
}

#[test]
fn source_action_selection_precedes_scenario_file_read() {
    let files = Files::new();
    for (source, action, expected) in [
        (
            "invoice.mori",
            "absent_action",
            "mori::source6::unknown_action",
        ),
        (
            "repayment.mori",
            "repay_loan",
            "mori::source6::unsupported_operation",
        ),
        (
            "oracle.mori",
            "read_fixing",
            "mori::source6::unsupported_operation",
        ),
    ] {
        let output = files.invoke(&[
            "expand",
            source,
            "--action",
            action,
            "--scenario",
            "absent.json",
            "--emit-source6-transfer",
        ]);
        assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(1));
        assert!(output.stdout.is_empty());
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
        assert!(stderr.contains(expected), "{stderr}");
        assert!(!stderr.contains("could not read"));
    }
}

#[test]
fn scenario_profile_and_subset_have_explicit_consumer_diagnostics() {
    let files = Files::new();
    let base: Value = serde_json::from_slice(fixture!("invoice.scenario.json")).unwrap();
    let foreign: Value = serde_json::from_slice(fixture!("core.scenario.json")).unwrap();
    let mut with_override = base.clone();
    with_override["candidate_effects"] = serde_json::json!([]);
    let mut with_obligation = base.clone();
    with_obligation["obligation"] = serde_json::json!({});
    let mut missing_cell = base;
    missing_cell["balances"].as_array_mut().unwrap().pop();
    for (scenario, expected) in [
        (foreign, "mori::command::source6-scenario-profile"),
        (with_override, "mori::command::source6-scenario-unsupported"),
        (
            with_obligation,
            "mori::command::source6-scenario-unsupported",
        ),
        (missing_cell, "mori::command::source6-scenario-cells"),
    ] {
        fs::write(
            files.0.join("scenario.json"),
            serde_json::to_vec(&scenario).unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let output = files.invoke(&source6_arguments());
        assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(1));
        assert!(output.stdout.is_empty());
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).contains(expected));
    }
}

#[test]
fn diagnostic_presentation_escapes_filename_action_and_scenario_shape_errors() {
    let files = Files::new();
    let hostile_file = "invoice\u{1b}\u{202e}.mori";
    fs::write(files.0.join(hostile_file), fixture!("invoice.mori")).unwrap();

    let unknown = files.invoke(&[
        "expand",
        hostile_file,
        "--action",
        "pay\n\u{1b}\u{202e}",
        "--scenario",
        "absent.json",
        "--emit-source6-transfer",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(unknown.status.code(), Some(1));
    assert!(unknown.stdout.is_empty());
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&unknown.stderr);
    assert!(stderr.contains("mori::source6::unknown_action"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(stderr.contains(r"invoice\u{1b}\u{202e}.mori"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(
        stderr.contains(r"No checked action named `pay\n\u{1b}\u{202e}` was found."),
        "{stderr}"
    );
    assert!(!stderr.contains(['\u{1b}', '\u{202e}']), "{stderr}");

    let mut bad_serde: Value = serde_json::from_slice(fixture!("invoice.scenario.json")).unwrap();
    bad_serde["replay"] = serde_json::json!("bad\u{1b}\u{202e}");
    fs::write(
        files.0.join("scenario.json"),
        serde_json::to_vec(&bad_serde).unwrap(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let shape = files.invoke(&source6_arguments());
    assert_eq!(shape.status.code(), Some(1));
    assert!(shape.stdout.is_empty());
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&shape.stderr);
    assert!(
        stderr.contains("mori::command::source6-scenario-shape"),
        "{stderr}"
    );
    assert!(stderr.contains(r"bad\u{1b}\u{202e}"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(!stderr.contains(['\u{1b}', '\u{202e}']), "{stderr}");

    let mut bad_domain: Value = serde_json::from_slice(fixture!("invoice.scenario.json")).unwrap();
    bad_domain["domain"] = serde_json::json!("Other");
    fs::write(
        files.0.join("scenario.json"),
        serde_json::to_vec(&bad_domain).unwrap(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let mismatch = files.invoke(&[
        "expand",
        hostile_file,
        "--action",
        "pay",
        "--scenario",
        "scenario.json",
        "--emit-source6-transfer",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(mismatch.status.code(), Some(1));
    assert!(mismatch.stdout.is_empty());
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&mismatch.stderr);
    assert!(stderr.contains("mori::source6::scenario_shape"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(stderr.contains(r"invoice\u{1b}\u{202e}.mori"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(!stderr.contains(['\u{1b}', '\u{202e}']), "{stderr}");
}

<BEGIN X062>
# Rust beta Source/6 transfer expansion

Status: ordinary interface adopted by the [2026-10-18 root decision](../evidence/utxo/doctorwatson-language-loop-2026-10-17/source6-public-consumer-adoption-20261018/DESIGN-ADOPTION.json). Source integration/audit and actual runtime remain UNRUN or pending; no compile, real-lowerer, security, native or release qualification is established. The `source6-expansion` Cargo feature enables the explicit local transfer presentation path; it is separate from `native` and does not alter default features.

Existing default command, unchanged:

```sh
mori expand core.mori --action noop --scenario core.json
```

This still validates a Core action against its Core scenario and prints its generic Core Program JSON. A Rust beta file supplied without the new option still reaches the existing Core parser and refuses; no default beta output is replaced. The separate Node beta package and its default JSON expansion output are unchanged.

Adopted explicit command interface, in a build with `source6-expansion` enabled:

```sh
mori check invoice.mori --json
mori --quiet expand invoice.mori --action pay --scenario scenario.json --emit-source6-transfer
```

The explicit command reads a typed local transfer scenario and first calls `mori-source6::select_transfer`, which uses the real Rust beta parser and checker, before reading the scenario file. The resulting `SelectedTransfer::expand` is the same emission path used by the `expand_transfer` convenience API. Stdout is the actual generated Source/6 text with its existing final newline; `--quiet` leaves stderr empty. Without `--quiet`, stderr reports `Expanded Source/6 transfer proposal (local-stipulation-only)`. It does not emit a Core success result. Without the build feature, the explicit option reports `mori::command::source6-unavailable`.

Source/action checking and unsupported selection precede scenario I/O. After strict JSON parsing, profile/kind is checked before closed transfer decoding; `obligation` and `candidate_effects` produce `source6-scenario-unsupported`, a non-three balance array produces `source6-scenario-cells`, and other DTO-shape errors produce `source6-scenario-shape`. Foreign/missing profile/kind produces `source6-scenario-profile`. These are ordinary command diagnostic categories, not Core judgments.

The adopted scenario JSON interface is the closed **transfer subset** of the existing `moriarty-local-scenario/1` / `local-stipulation` shape. It requires domain, asset, head, predecessor, round, exactly three ordered balances, allowance, replay, work_remaining, work_spent and post_head. Numeric values are canonical decimal strings parsed through the existing Core UInt decoder; no new decimal evaluator is introduced. Balance order is owner, recipient, fee recipient. Replay is `unused` or `consumed`. Obligation and candidate_effects overrides are outside this option. The current strict CLI reader and existing read/JSON bounds apply.

The root decision adopts this profile-token reuse, transfer subset, option name, feature name, raw stdout/status output and public diagnostic classifications as the exact ordinary interface. The two original design reviews and their historical wording remain unchanged in the decision record. Adoption does not establish full Node beta wire or diagnostic parity. The typed borrowed local scenario passed to the library is an internal input, not proof or authentication.

Evidence remains separate: the existing independent14 financial payload baseline predates this actual consumer. Same-author pre-code fixture/snapshot files remain author baselines; complete new wire/output/work expectations and the chosen WorkshopReceipt fixture freeze are still missing. Public binary checks, actual emitted Rust bytes through `parseAndLowerSource6`, ordinary source/result audits and the designated owner's filename/security judgment remain unrun or pending.

Boundary: Rust beta/1 → local transfer proposal presentation → Source/6 text. The real experimental TypeScript `parseAndLowerSource6` must still consume actual emitted bytes; its Core/5 preparation remains separately unqualified. This option provides no Source/6/Core/5→Core/1/Core/2/Sherlock/native embedding, no handwritten target IR and no target/proof/post-state success. The default Core and separate Node consumers retain their own profiles.
<END X062>

# Core continuations

`moriarty/2` adds typed suspension and resumption to Rust Core. An action can
return a local prefix and a continuation, then evaluate its remaining statements
when supplied a typed event. Existing `moriarty/1` programs retain their atomic
semantics, JSON and logical-cost profile.

Current selected evidence covers **88 distinct focused Rust test functions**:
17 functions passed in the last closure captures (12 public CLI and 5 Core
compatibility cases). Another 71 functions are retained on unchanged selected
call paths: 40 other Core, 15 backend normal/relation, 9 ledger closure/profile,
6 backend frame and 1 legacy byte-comparison case. This is not a fresh rerun of
all 88 functions. See
[closure observations](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/OBSERVATIONS-CLOSURE.json)
and [closure source scope](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/SOURCE-SCOPE-CLOSURE.json)
for the selections and retained-evidence basis. The candidate remains local and
unmerged; final closure Muse and Opus source/result reviews are pending.

Historical candidate `dd4` covered 86 distinct functions: 24 freshly captured
and 62 retained. Its
[observations](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/OBSERVATIONS-FINAL.json)
and [source scope](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/SOURCE-SCOPE-FINAL.json)
retain that earlier scope.

Historical successor `7d6c3965` covered 78 distinct functions: 49 freshly captured
and 29 carried forward. Its
[observations](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/OBSERVATIONS-CURRENT.json)
and [source scope](audits/2026-10-15/core-continuations/SOURCE-SCOPE-CURRENT.json)
retain that earlier scope.

Separate Quint QA totals 11 normal tests: 2 prefix tests and 9 lifecycle tests,
with 4 prefix one-transition samples and 32 sampled lifecycle traces. These
model results are excluded from the Rust total; Rust correspondence remains
unestablished.

Historical candidate `e9a2b80b` recorded **58 focused Rust tests passed**: 32 Core tests (5 normal,
4 compatibility, 13 static-cost and 10 hostile), 7 public CLI tests, 5 backend
normal tests, 4 backend relation tests, 6 backend frame tests, 3 ledger closure
tests and 1 baseline byte-comparison test. The CLI tests include compilation,
publication and reopening for both specimens. Captures are `core-normal-01`, `core-compat-01`,
`core-static-cost-01`, `core-hostile-01`, `cli-normal-02`, `backend-normal-02`,
`backend-relation-01`, `backend-frame-01`, `ledger-source-closure-01` and
`legacy-byte-comparator-01` in the 2026-10-15 continuation runtime evidence.
The comparator was ignored in
the normal backend run and then passed separately. Source and baseline dependency
pins remained unchanged; the captures recorded zero requested native actions.

For the independently frozen compatibility specimen only, a baseline generated
by the preserved PR52 binary matched the candidate's `/3` manifest and every IR
file byte-for-byte. Exact export and fixture leaf sets and hashes were checked
before and after. This is a bounded compatibility result. Separately, the first
Quint increment passed 2 normal tests and 4 witness traces; it is normal model QA,
with Rust correspondence still unestablished. Full source and actual-result
reviews remain due. Native-call execution through `mori-ledger` does not support
`/2`. No U0–U7, M1–M17 or MC/SP/G exit is closed by this evidence.

## Write an await

The [delivery example](../examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori) contains:

```mori
language "moriarty/2";
agreement ContinuationEscrowOracle {
  asset PAY = { network: "local", issuer: "continuation-escrow-oracle", reference: "PAY", scale: 0 };
  state marker: UInt = 77;
  action deliver(amount: UInt) {
    transfer(PAY, "alice", "escrow", amount);
    liability("release", PAY, "escrow", "bob", amount);
    await delivery(ready: Bool) when ready;
    transfer(PAY, "escrow", "bob", amount);
    discharge("release", amount);
  }
}
```

`delivery` names this await site. Its event declares a Bool named `ready`; the
guard has type Bool. Event binders may use Bool or UInt. Labels are unique within
an action, and binders cannot shadow existing names. The current bounds are
16 awaits per action, 16 event binders per site and 256 capture slots.

Reaching the await ends the current segment before evaluating its guard. With
the supplied scenario (`amount` = 10), the local prefix has balances `alice` 90,
`escrow` 10 and `bob` 0, plus a `release` duty of 10. The remaining transfer and
discharge have not run.
`requires` and `ensures` remain assertions at their source positions; a false
assertion does not become an await.

## Start and resume through the CLI

From the repository root, the start interface is:

```sh
mori simulate examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --action deliver \
  --scenario examples/core/continuations/delivery-scenario.json \
  --logical-cap 11
```

Save the result's **`continuation` member alone** as `continuation.json`.
Resume takes that object, not the full waiting report or a segment history.

```sh
mori simulate examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --resume continuation.json \
  --event examples/core/continuations/delivery-false-resume.json

mori simulate examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --resume continuation.json \
  --event examples/core/continuations/delivery-true-resume-complete.json
```

A false guard returns `status:"waiting"`, `advanced:false`, `segment:null` and
the unchanged continuation. It produces no new prefix. A true guard runs only
the remainder: the delivery example reaches balances `alice` 90, `escrow` 0 and
`bob` 10, and retains the `release` duty present with amount 0. Funding is not
repeated.

An event file supplies an ordered, named, typed tuple:

```json
{"format":"moriarty-stage-event/1","action":"deliver","label":"delivery","values":[{"name":"ready","value":{"type":"Bool","value":true}}]}
```

`--resume` requires `--event` and conflicts with `--scenario`, `--trace`,
`--target` and authorization arguments. An optional resume `--action` must
match the continuation. `--logical-cap` is optional on start and resume.
Waiting and complete results exit with status 0; rejected stages exit with
status 1. A rejected suffix
returns its error and attempted work, with no segment or replacement
continuation; the prior local prefix and input continuation remain available.

The stored `continuation.logical.cap` is outside both continuation digests,
`program_hash` and `plan_hash`. A caller can edit it, remove it or raise it,
and resume will not detect the change. Treat it as a local advisory ceiling.
It is not an authenticated lifetime work budget. Resume still checks that
`logical.committed` matches the planned prefix work for the stored `site`.
An optional resume `--logical-cap` must not exceed a present stored cap. The
effective cap, which is that flag when given and otherwise the stored cap,
must cover `committed` plus the next segment. None of these
checks authenticates the continuation or records its consumption.

Every staged JSON report and `/4` manifest carries the Opus-authored labels exactly:

```json
{"qualification":"local-reference-stage","authentication":"none","consumption":"untracked"}
```

The [Opus-authored stage contract](../crates/mori-core/src/stage/mod.rs) records
their scope. Consult the [security ownership record](audits/2026-10-14/SECURITY-ROUTING.md)
and the separately scoped [Opus security review](audits/2026-10-14/SECURITY-REVIEW.md)
for security analysis. This guide describes language and tool behavior.

## What survives a boundary

Action inputs and evaluated lets are captured by value. Earlier accepted event
binders are captured for later awaits. State and liabilities are read from the
current boundary. To retain a state value as it stood earlier, bind it explicitly,
for example `let savedBasis = basis;`.

The [two-await reserve example](../examples/core/continuations/reserve.mori)
starts with `basis` 40 and `extra` 2. It captures `held` 42, then updates `basis`
to 35. The accepted event value `quote` 43 remains available after the second
await; `basis` has meanwhile become 78. The final segment uses `held` 42 and
`quote` 43 rather than recomputing them from `basis` 78. Completion retains an
allocation duty of 5.

`residual` lists every positive liability in the post boundary. Completing an
action does not erase those duties or report settlement. Each awaiting action
has one pending frame in the staged representation; the local qualifications
above remain part of every result.

## Logical work and compilation

The profile is `moriarty-reference-logical-cost/2`. It counts statement dispatch
and distinct expression-node visits with a fresh cache per statement. A plan
records the successful cost of each segment. Reaching an await charges its entry;
resuming charges dispatch and evaluates the guard.

For delivery, start costs 5 and a true resume costs 6, for 11 committed units.
A false resume reports 2 attempted units while committed work remains 5. A later
true resume still completes at 11 committed units. Reserve has segment costs
11, 15 and 10, for 36 committed units. Attempted work on a false or rejected
invocation is reported separately.

These units are not circuit cost, DUST, service fees or proof measurements.
The unsigned compiler source path emits `/4` staged artifacts with `N + 1` circuits
for N awaits; a false observation has no circuit. Zero-await `/2` actions have
one circuit. The CLI compilation interface is:

```sh
mori compile examples/core/continuations/delivery.mori \
  --target target.json --out new-output-directory
```

The target is supplied separately. Staged manifests and ZKIR source retain their
unperformed qualification gates. The local CLI results above do not establish
native proof or target qualification.

## Rust API

Use [`mori_core::stage`](../crates/mori-core/src/stage/mod.rs):

```rust
let program = mori_core::stage::load(source)?;
let outcome = mori_core::stage::start(&program, "deliver", scenario, Some(mori_core::UInt(11)))?;
// Match StageOutcome::Waiting to obtain its Continuation.
let next = mori_core::stage::resume(&program, continuation, event, None, None)?;
```

`StagedProgram` exposes its parsed program and plan through read-only getters.
`StageOutcome` distinguishes Waiting and Complete; its segments include frame
pre/post values and an Execution with original source statement indices.
`StageRejection` contains error, attempted and committed work. Legacy `parse`,
`validate` and `simulate` remain `/1` entry points.
<END X063>

## X064: docs/DOCTORWATSON.md

Whole-body SHA256: b1777954c14042333683dc464cdd6a838be69f1682ed5e7483bffddb62d5d5ba; bytes: 12489; delivery: full.

<BEGIN X064>
# DoctorWatson: the Sherlock software factory

Current working plan, 2026-10-16. The user names the factory **DoctorWatson**;
Sherlock is the universal interpreter it builds. The user authorizes building and running this
factory and requires **local CI**, because hosted CI is too expensive. GitHub
stores source, PRs and result summaries. No Foreman or replacement scheduler is
used. The [research review](research/sherlock/factory-2026-10-16/README.md)
records the nine planning reviews and ten online research assignments.

The default executable lane checks the independent A-profile corpus and its
committed source transcription. The explicit `--host` lane builds and executes
the actual Sherlock host reference, exercises bounded stepping and compares its
complete normal observations with those expectations. These are distinct
developer QA jobs; neither establishes the remaining cross-layer correspondence.
See the [local commands](DOCTORWATSON-CI.md), the QA
[contract](../models/sherlock/qa/CONTRACT.md), and the
[factory EARS](../openspec/changes/doctorwatson/requirements.md).

The [parallel delivery results](audits/2026-10-16/sherlock-parallel-delivery/README.md)
now include actual Rust host, flat-ID image and Quint observations against the
same independently frozen eight-program corpus. Each matches all 216 prefixes
and 5,355 complete records. All 14 selected Rust host tests pass; image tests
were not selected. The new continuation tests cover all 204 N03–N08 prefixes,
every event cut and widths 1/2/4/8. A captured regression also fixes selection of
the correct fuel run in raw divergence diagnostics. K decoding and supplied
Lean comparison are implemented consumers; their presence does not establish
actual K or Lean execution. Source-Core and streaming execution are separate
increments, outside those recorded captures.

Lessons for the later factory update are kept in the
[DoctorWatson improvement log](../wiki-llm/doctorwatson-improvement-log.md).
Append after material Sherlock iterations; distinguish proposed changes, applied
source and validated behavior.

## One delivery cycle

1. Select an unchecked feature in the existing
   [Sherlock plan](SHERLOCK-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md) or current
   [A-machine status](../openspec/changes/sherlock-machine-circuit-layout/IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS-2026-10-16.md).
   Name its existing requirement/rule, actual consumer and observable result.
2. Assign disjoint paths and an owner. Freeze independent expected observations
   before executing the implementation. Shared interfaces belong to one integrator.
3. Implement the smallest useful consumer increment. Run local ordinary checks
   and the affected separately admitted K, Quint and Lean/Clean checks. Record
   missing layers as gaps. Witness generation and constraint checks are separate.
4. Compare complete states, prefixes, charges, outcomes and relevant ordered
   financial effects. Preserve the first failing input and field difference.
   Repair from the semantic contract, rather than replacing the expected result.
5. Give a fresh non-author reviewer the full candidate and actual results.
   Integrate through a normal GitHub PR; repeat affected local checks after
   integration changes. Report source, observations and acceptance separately.

Local CI is an explicit command, not a daemon. Agents run it when their changed
closure requires it. It never dispatches model/proof/ledger work implicitly.
After two failures of the same defect class, reduce the reproducer and change
approach. After two process-only cycles or thirty administration minutes, return
to eligible implementation or name the concrete blocker and owner.

## Exact candidate and dependency freshness

Use Git's candidate commit/tree and integration-base identity in the PR, alongside
the applicable profile, bounds, oracle/projection and tool/command identities.
These identify the inputs actually checked; a task label is insufficient.
Keep original outputs and their digests with the result, including failure and
timeout. A passing checker is not a successful later test command.
Each attempt also has its own identity. A result must match both the candidate
fingerprint and the current attempt; retrying unchanged source cannot admit a
late result from the timed-out or cancelled attempt.

An edit to any consumed input invalidates the affected results and reviews.
Declared dependencies include shared schemas, profiles, expectations, adapters,
test/import membership, entrypoints and integration wiring. Follow those edges
transitively; a missing dependency declaration is a process limitation, not
evidence that nothing changed. A merge changes the integration base. Before the
next merge, recheck the candidate against that base, refresh the affected
comparisons and obtain review of the resulting tree and actual results.

Source-only integration can explicitly retain unrun higher tiers; it cannot mark
the feature behavior, cross-layer correspondence or parent exit complete. An
available tool/layer is not an observation. Cancelled or blocked tasks release
their active write ownership and retain historical failures and results.
Upstream edits invalidate their candidate evidence without reactivating those
terminal dispositions or clearing their recorded administration/failure history.
Reactivation needs an explicit owner decision outside this finite delivery cycle.

The [DoctorWatson Quint model](../models/doctorwatson/README.md) checks these
workflow transitions on a small concrete task/actor instance. It is a model of
the design, not a scheduler or proof that agents/Git execute the design faithfully.

## Parallel ownership

Use the available session slots for independent ready work. There is no fixed
three- or six-lane ceiling. More workers help only while write sets, review,
integration and physical resources remain available. Source concurrency changes
no execution authority or resource counter.

| Work | Owner | Useful Luna support |
|---|---|---|
| Shared profiles, IR, ABI, exports and consumers | Integrator | Source/field maps and call-site inventories |
| Nonsecurity implementation | GPT-6.1 Sol high | Precisely specified fixture transcription and narrow leaf changes under an expert contract |
| Independent normal expectations | Non-author oracle owner | Hand calculations from frozen semantics, checked independently before use |
| Security work and judgments | Opus 5.5, with the existing outage fallback | Gather exact source locators; do not decide constraints or security outcomes |
| Nonsecurity candidate/result audit | Fresh Muse Wonder 1.0 high | Link/coverage inventories; no substitute approval |
| Private Lean/Clean integration | Existing Fenrir fork owner | Public scope crosswalks; private sources and paths stay private |

Each assignment records the requirement, predicate, exact paths, consumer,
dependencies, oracle owner, applicable checks, first blocked boundary and expected
deliverable. A reviewer does not author the implementation or derive expectations
from its output. Luna tasks return bounded files and unresolved choices, rather
than repeatedly reading the whole repository. Track useful integrated behavior,
review delay, repeated defects and actual check duration; agent count is not
completion.

## Sprint sequence

These are execution slices of the existing roadmap, not replacement milestones.
Advance ready independent source tasks in parallel; acceptance retains dependencies.

| Slice | Concrete output and acceptance test | Parallel preparation | Retained blocker |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current: local QA foundation | One local command validates the frozen eight-case corpus, checks committed source readback, and reports incomplete or different supplied observations | Local command/docs; independent checker tests; source/task maps | No actual K/Quint/Lean/Clean/circuit execution follows from this check |
| Current: first real Sherlock build | Explicit local host build, new `Machine::run_steps`, normal cut/resume tests and all 216 complete prefix observations through the actual consumer | Reference API; fixed typed inputs/exporter; independent literal projection; real CLI regressions; Opus wrapper | Host post-startup common domain only; constructor startup and model/circuit/native layers stay separate |
| Current: factory design audit | Quint scenarios and sampled workflow traces check SF-01–15, candidate/attempt freshness, ownership, CI fail-stop and integration | Independent requirements checklist and source performance review | This models the factory's design; real agent/Git compliance and interpreter correctness remain separate |
| Existing A arithmetic/fuel QA | Finish adjudicating the already captured 18-test attempt; run the existing separately admitted sampled phase once only if its postgates pass | K source review and normal literal maps; G4 source analysis | No rerun of terminal attempts; K execution and full relation correspondence remain open |
| Reference and model adapters | Map one declared common domain to complete typed observations and earliest differing prefix | Independent fixtures; K field map; finite Quint map; existing Lean reconciliation | Profile clocks differ; absent layers cannot count as agreement |
| Bounded state and helpers | Complete the existing rule/representation decisions and source consumers for data, frames, arithmetic and immutable append | Disjoint host codecs, oracle derivations and operation inventories | Candidate B schemas require their existing decision; A P1–P6 is a separate scope |
| Handwritten and Clean components | Same admitted step projected through independently bound witness and constraint implementations | Component inventories and source preparation within existing authority | C4 requires admitted A102 compilation before dependent circuit edits; native authority is zero |
| Witness/export and resources | Actual consumer reports supported operations and separate witness/constraint export, logical work and physical costs | Witness DAG, exporter capability and resource adapters after their interfaces stabilize | Unknown physical costs are unknown, not zero; source inventory is not native support |
| Optimization | Batch/resume/cache/residual implementations preserve every internal prefix and earliest stop against baseline | Independent width 1/2/4/8 expectations and cut/resume cases | Stable semantics and complete observation adapters first |
| Financial compiler mapping | Two contrasting supported programs preserve full ordered effects, work, fees, liabilities and residual duties | Independent source programs and finance expectations | General compiler/continuation mapping and target phase semantics remain open |
| Native and Midnight stagenet | Sherlock itself compiles, proves, verifies, deploys, calls and reads back complete state/effects on the qualified target | Source integration and operator-supplied non-secret target facts | Existing execution admission, exact toolchain/target tuple and required security evidence |

For each slice update the existing correctness-loop evidence matrix: source and
profile, independent oracle, actual command/exit, raw output digest, per-layer
status, first divergence and next concrete action. Keep failed results. Do not
merge unrelated historical test cohorts into one completion denominator.

## Full V1 remains downstream

Sherlock supports Moriarty's [U0–U7 roadmap](../ROADMAP.md); it does not replace it.
Retain M1–M17, MC/SP/G exits, general source-to-ZKIRv3 correspondence, recursive
and private history, all five composition operators, lifecycle/recovery, fee and
federation policy, ACTUS/DeFi conformance and independent developer release.
The financial inventory distinguishes 276 ACTUS contract cases plus AD0 analysis
from the 277 aggregate, and retains the unresolved ANN file-count discrepancy.
The 160 canonical headings, 15 separate OSR clauses and 35 Sherlock EARS are
indices, not atomic completion percentages. Every full parent exit remains open.

K, Quint and Lean/Clean are required iterative developer QA alongside handwritten
circuits. They are not public compiler/runtime/prover dependencies. Midnight
stagenet acceptance is required for Sherlock; Preview or Fenrir observations
cannot replace it. Do not invent Fenrir identities or network versioning.
All native limits, C4, counters and terminal results remain unchanged. Project
review does not become permission for a developer to use Moriarty.
